example: This Halloween we were greeted at our door by werewolves, mummies, and a wide assortment of sweet-toothed hobgoblins.

definition: Truculent describes a person who is easily annoyed and eager to argue or fight. It can also describe the mood or attitude of such a person.
example: The approach of multiple deadlines had put me in a truculent mood, and I could tell my colleagues were avoiding me.

definition: Deliquesce can mean "to dissolve or melt away" or, in reference to some fungal structures (such as mushroom gills), "to become soft or liquid with age or maturity."
example: The mushrooms deliquesced into an inky fluid.

definition: Menagerie refers to a collection of animals kept especially to be shown to the public, as well as a place where such animals are kept. It can also refer figuratively to any varied mixture of things.
example: The aviary featured a menagerie of exotic birds.

definition: Something described as acerbic is sharply or bitingly critical, sarcastic, or ironic in temper, mood, or tone.
example: The comedian draws crowds that appreciate his acerbic wit.

definition: Cognoscente refers to a person with expert knowledge in a subject. It is usually encountered in its plural form, cognoscenti, and preceded by the.
example: The audience at the club, though small, was full of writers, musicians, and other noteworthy members of the jazz cognoscenti.

definition: Wreak means “to cause something very harmful or damaging.” It is often used with on or upon.
example: The virus wreaked havoc on my laptop.

definition: Rancid usually describes something edible that has a strong and unpleasant smell or taste because it is no longer fresh. In figurative use, rancid describes things that are very distasteful or offensive.
example: The corpse flower, which is the largest known individual flower of any plant species, stays open five to seven days and emits a rancid odor.

definition: Litany usually refers to a long list of complaints, problems, etc. It can also refer to a sizable series or set, a lengthy recitation, a repetitive chant, or a particular kind of call-and-response prayer.
example: Among the television critic’s litany of complaints about the new series is the anachronistic costume design.

definition: To frolic is to play and move about happily.
example: We watched the seals as they frolicked in the harbor.

definition: Something described as sedentary does or involves a lot of sitting. Sedentary can also mean "not physically active" (as in "a sedentary lifestyle") or "not migratory" (as in "sedentary birds" or "a sedentary civilization").
example: Editing the dictionary is a sedentary job.

definition: An etymology is an explanation of a word’s history—that is, where the word came from and how it developed.
example: As a word nerd, I’m always eager to learn a word’s etymology and trace it back to its earliest known origins.

definition: Veritable is a formal adjective that means “being in fact the thing named and not false, unreal, or imaginary.” It is often used to stress the aptness of a metaphorical description.
example: The island is a veritable paradise.

definition: When muse is used to mean "to think about something carefully or thoroughly," it is usually followed by about, on, over, or upon. The word can also mean "to become absorbed in thought," or "to think or say something in a thoughtful way."
example: He mused on the possibility of pursuing a master's degree.

definition: Kibosh refers to something that serves as a check or stop. It is usually used in the phrase “put the kibosh on” to mean “to stop or end (something)” or “to prevent (something) from happening or continuing.”
example: I downloaded an app to help me put the kibosh on my high screen time.

definition: Biannual is an adjective used to describe something that happens twice a year, or something that happens every two years.
example: The art show is a biannual event that won’t happen again for two more years.

definition: To coalesce is to come together to form one group or mass.
example: The club’s community service projects provide students with a common goal to coalesce around.

definition: Utopia refers to an imaginary place in which the government, laws, and social conditions are perfect; a utopia is a place of ideal perfection.
example: It’s a nice place to live, but it’s no utopia.

definition: Penultimate means "occurring immediately before the last one," or in other words, "next to last." A formal adjective, it is always used before the noun it modifies.
example: The penultimate episode of the TV series features some shocking plot twists that set up what will surely be a thrilling series finale.

definition: Imprimatur is a formal word that refers to explicit approval or permission.
example: Though not an official project of the theater, the drama festival has its imprimatur.

definition: Something described as languid shows or has very little energy, force, or activity.
example: We paddled at a languid pace, in no hurry to arrive at our picnic destination.

definition: To obviate something (usually a need for something, or a necessity) is to anticipate and prevent it. A formal word, obviate can also mean "to make an action unnecessary."
example: The new medical treatment obviates the need for surgery.

definition: Duress, which is typically used with under, refers to force or threats meant to make someone do something. It is used especially of unlawful coercion.
example: The defense asserts that the defendant’s confession was made under duress.

definition: Finicky describes someone who is very hard to please, or something that requires a lot of care, precision, or attentive effort.
example: Although she was a finicky eater as a child, she grew up to become a world-renowned chef famous for her encyclopedic knowledge of global ingredients.

definition: Candor refers to the quality of being open, sincere, and honest.
example: During the interview, the comedian spoke with candor about the nervousness she feels every time she takes the stage.

definition: To embarrass someone is to make them feel confused and foolish in front of other people.
example: Unexpected laughter embarrassed the speaker.

definition: Sonorous is an adjective used in formal speech and writing to describe something that has a deep, loud, and pleasant sound. Sonorous can also mean “producing sound (when struck)” and “imposing or impressive in effect or style.”
example: The baritone’s deep, sonorous voice cut through the din of the crowd, the voices immediately halting their conversations to listen more intently.

definition: Repertoire typically refers to a list or supply of plays, songs, dances, etc. that a company or person is prepared to perform,. Repertoire may also refer to a supply of skills or devices, or more broadly to an amount or supply.
example: The band's repertoire includes both classic and modern jazz.

definition: Gibbous is most often used to describe the moon or a planet when it is seen with more than half but not all of the apparent disk illuminated.
example: The waxing gibbous moon provided the perfect lighting for a night of spooky storytelling around the campfire.

definition: To atone for something is to make amends for it—that is, to do something good as a way of showing that you are sorry about, or have remorse for, a mistake, bad behavior, etc.
example: The novel opens with an act of cruelty and then traces the thoughts and actions of those responsible as they try to atone for it.

definition: Preternatural is a formal adjective used to describe things that are very unusual in a way that does not seem natural.
example: He has a preternatural knack for imitating birdcalls.

definition: Impetuous is a synonym of impulsive that describes a person who is acting without thought, or an action that is done without thought.
example: That impetuous decision could've cost us everything we worked so hard for.

definition: To obliterate something is to destroy it completely so that nothing is left, to destroy utterly all trace, indication, or significance of it. It can also mean "to remove utterly from recognition or memory."
example: The wave completely obliterated our sandcastles.

definition: Kerfuffle is an informal word that refers to a disturbance or fuss typically caused by a dispute or conflict.
example: The reclassification of Pluto from a planet to a dwarf planet caused quite a kerfuffle among astronomy lovers.

definition: Vociferous describes people who express their feelings or opinions loudly and insistently. It is also applied to things, such as objections, that are expressed in such a way.
example: We were vociferous in our support of the proposal.

definition: Gesundheit is an interjection used to wish good health to one who has just sneezed.
example: I sneezed three times in a row, and my coworker called "gesundheit!" from the next cubicle.

definition: Anomaly is a somewhat formal word that refers to something that is remarkable in its deviation from what is usual or expected.
example: Last summer’s storm was an anomaly for this area.

definition: To brandish something, such as a weapon, is to wave or swing it in a threatening or excited manner.
example: Squeals of laughter erupted as three children brandishing squirt guns rounded the corner of the house.

definition: Nonpareil describes that which has no equal because it is better than any other.
example: To this day, the band's debut album is still considered nonpareil, raising the bar for every rock group to follow.

definition: Catch-22 typically refers to a difficult situation for which there is no easy or possible solution. In the narrowest use of the term, it refers to a problematic situation for which the only solution is denied by a circumstance inherent in the problem or by a rule.
example: I’m in a catch-22: to get the job I need experience, but how do I get experience if I can’t get the job?

definition: Lugubrious is a formal word used chiefly to describe something that is very sad especially in an exaggerated or insincere way. The word can also describe something that shows or expresses gloom.
example: The movie’s stunning cinematography could not make up for the lugubrious and plodding plot.

definition: Enmity is a formal word that refers to a very deep unfriendly feeling, such as hatred or ill will, that is often felt mutually.
example: Having to collaborate on the project only increased the bitter enmity between the two coworkers, who had never gotten along.

definition: Succumbing is about yielding to something: someone who succumbs to a pressure or emotion stops trying to resist that pressure or emotion, and someone who succumbs to an injury or disease dies because of that injury or disease. The word is often followed by to.
example: The program aims to help kids develop the strength of character required to avoid succumbing to peer pressure.

definition: Rationale refers to an explanation or reason for something said or done. It is often used with for, behind, or of.
example: City council members who oppose the zoning change should be ready to explain their rationale for voting against it.

definition: Jovial describes people as well as moods, attitudes, etc., that are cheerful and jolly.
example: The audience was in a jovial mood as the headlining comedian walked onto the stage.

definition: To debunk something (such as a belief or theory) is to show that it is not true.
example: The influencer remained enormously popular despite having the bulk of their health claims thoroughly debunked.

definition: Askance means "in a way that shows a lack of trust or approval" or "with a side-glance."
example: I couldn't help but look askance at the dealer's assurances that the car had never been in an accident.

definition: Perpetuity refers to a state of continuing forever or for a very long time.
example: The property will be passed on from generation to generation in perpetuity.

definition: Someone or something described as consummate is very skilled or accomplished. Consummate  can also mean “of the highest degree” and “complete in every detail.” The adjective is always used before the noun it describes.
example: Ever the consummate professional, the planner ensured that no one attending the event was aware of all the elements that had not gone as planned.

definition: To flummox someone is to confuse or perplex them.
example: The actor was easily flummoxed by last-minute changes to the script.

definition: Zoomorphic describes things that have the form of an animal.
example: The local bakery is famous for its wide variety of zoomorphic treats, from “hedgehog” dinner rolls to delicate, swan-shaped pastries.

definition: The term griot refers to any of a class of musician-entertainers of western Africa whose performances include tribal histories and genealogies. The term is also used broadly to refer to a storyteller.
example: Tracing her family lineage back to West African griots inspired the singer to focus on storytelling through her music.

definition: To insinuate something (especially something bad or insulting) is to say it in a subtle or indirect way. Insinuate can also mean "to gradually make (oneself) a part of a group, a person's life, etc., often by behaving in a dishonest way."
example: When the teacher questioned the students about their identical test answers, they knew she was insinuating that they had cheated.

definition: Sanguine is a formal word that today almost always describes someone who is confident and hopeful, or something that shows confidence and hopefulness. Sanguine can also describe something that is bloodred in color, something involving or relating to bloodshed, or a person’s reddish complexion.
example: The young group of entrepreneurs is sanguine about the future of their business.

definition: Behest can refer either to an authoritative order or an urgent prompting.
example: The committee met again at the senator’s behest.

definition: To mollify someone is to make them less angry. Mollify can also mean "to reduce in intensity."
example: The celebrity's statement was intended to mollify critics.

definition: Histrionic is a word used disapprovingly to describe someone or something that is too emotional or dramatic.
example: The head chef had a penchant for dish throwing, door slamming, and other histrionic displays of temper whenever a dish was sent back to the kitchen.

definition: Abeyance is a formal word that is almost always used in the phrase “in abeyance” to describe something in a temporary state of inactivity—that is, something in a state of suspension.
example: The legal case is now being held in abeyance while the parties attempt to find a mutually acceptable solution.

definition: Something described as trivial is of little worth or importance.
example: Although her parents initially dismissed her love of pop music as a trivial matter, it became clear as she applied to colleges with strong popular music programs that much of her life was going to be dedicated to it.

definition: To carp is to complain in an annoying way.
example: They’re always carping about their boss.

definition: Epitome means "a perfect example." It is usually used in the phrase "the epitome of," as in "the epitome of elegance."
example: In his tailored suit and fashionable haircut, he was the very epitome of style.

definition: Simpatico typically describes two or more people or things with shared qualities, interests, etc. It can also describe someone who is agreeable or likeable.
example: Even though they weren’t always simpatico with regard to the direction of their company, the pair managed to be successful partners for more than 35 years.

definition: Protocol most often refers to a system of rules explaining the correct conduct and procedures to be followed in a formal situation; in computer programming a protocol is a set of rules used in formatting data. Protocol can also refer to a plan for a scientific experiment or medical treatment, or to a document that describes the details of a diplomatic treaty.
example: What is the proper protocol for declining a job offer?

definition: Incisive means "impressively direct and decisive." It is generally applied to either something communicated in a way that is very clear and direct, or to a person who is able to explain difficult ideas clearly and confidently.
example: The columnist is known for her incisive commentary on local politics.

definition: Diminution is a formal word that refers to the act or process of becoming less.
example: The company is committed to seeing that efforts to scale up production do not result in a diminution of quality.

definition: Nebulous is a formal word used to describe something that is difficult to see, understand, or describe—in other words, something indistinct or vague.
example: A lot of philosophical concepts can seem nebulous at first, but a good instructor can cut through the jargon and help students see how they apply to day-to-day life.

definition: Trepidation refers to a feeling of fear that causes someone to hesitate because they think that something bad or unpleasant is going to happen.
example: The students felt a sense of trepidation upon being summoned to the principal's office.

definition: Undulant describes things that rise and fall in waves, or things that have a wavy form, outline, or surface.
example: The exhibit featured a painting with beautiful green strokes that resembled undulant hills.

definition: To cloister someone or something is to shut the person or thing away from the world.
example: The scientist cloistered himself in his laboratory all weekend to finish analyzing data.

definition: Something may be described as flagrant if it is conspicuously bad—that is, too bad to be ignored.
example: In a flagrant violation of the family's code of ethics, someone finished the ice cream and left the empty container in the freezer.

definition: Apathy refers either to a lack of feeling or emotion, or to a lack of interest or concern.
example: Though the girl’s expression communicated apathy, Gina knew her daughter was actually very pleased at having won the poetry prize.

definition: To validate something is to show that it is real or correct. Validate can also mean “to state or show that something is legal or official,” “to put a mark on something to show that it has been checked and is official or accepted,” and “to show that someone’s feelings, opinions, etc., are fair and reasonable.”
example: The company’s claims about its latest product are yet to be validated.

definition: Something described as salient is very important or noticeable.
example: The assignment was to write down the most salient points made in the article.

definition: A euphemism is a mild or pleasant word or phrase that is used instead of one that is unpleasant or offensive.
example: The HR department advises using the euphemism “let go” instead of saying that someone was fired.

definition: Ostentatious describes someone or something that displays wealth, knowledge, power, etc., in a way that is meant to attract attention, admiration, or envy. Things that are ostentatious tend to stand out as overly elaborate or conspicuous.
example: The resort town is famous for its extravagantly expensive summer homes, which some tourists view as impressive and others as merely ostentatious.

definition: Glitch is an informal word referring to an unexpected and usually minor problem. It is used especially for a minor problem with a machine or device, such as a computer.
example: The email went out to everyone in the company because of a technical glitch.

definition: Tempestuous is used to describe something that is related to or resembles a violent storm. In its literal (and often literary) use tempestuous is synonymous with turbulent and stormy. Figuratively, tempestuous describes something or someone full of strong emotions, such as anger or excitement.
example: On its return to port the unlucky schooner was beset by tempestuous weather and nearly capsized.

definition: To meander is to follow a winding or intricate course—that is, one with a lot of turns and curves—or to walk slowly without a specific goal, purpose, or direction.
example: We spent the afternoon meandering around the seaside town.

definition: Immutable is a formal adjective used to describe something that is unable to be changed.
example: It is hardly an immutable fact that cats and dogs are sworn enemies; over the years our golden retriever has grown both fond and protective of her tabby housemate.

definition: Calculus refers to an advanced branch of mathematics that deals mostly with rates of change and with finding lengths, areas, and volumes. The word can also be used more broadly for the act of calculating—that is, estimating something by using practical judgment, or solving or probing the meaning of something.
example: By my calculus the more efficient air conditioner will have paid for itself within a span of five years.

definition: Ramshackle describes things that are in a very bad condition and need to be repaired, or that are carelessly or loosely constructed.
example: Toward the back of the property stood a ramshackle old shed.

definition: To stipulate is to demand or require something as part of an agreement.
example: The rules stipulate that players must wear uniforms.

definition: Someone or something described as hidebound is inflexible and unwilling to accept new or different ideas.
example: Although somewhat stuffy and strict, the professor did not so completely adhere to hidebound academic tradition that he wouldn’t teach class outside on an especially lovely day.

definition: A behemoth is something of monstrous size, power, or appearance. Behemoth (usually capitalized) is also the name of a mighty animal described in the biblical book of Job.
example: The town will be voting on whether or not to let the retail behemoth build a store on the proposed site.

definition: Winsome describes people and things that are cheerful, pleasant, and appealing.
example: Though a relative newcomer to acting, Maya won the casting directors over with her winsome charm, which was perfect for the role of the plucky young superhero.

definition: To adjudicate a dispute between two parties is to make an official decision about which party is right; to adjudicate a case or claim is to settle it judicially. Adjudicate is also used to mean “to act as judge.”
example: The case will be adjudicated in the state courts.

definition: Largesse is a somewhat formal word that refers to the act of giving away money or the generosity of a person who gives away money. It can also refer to the money that is given away.
example: The community has benefited greatly from the largesse of its wealthiest family.

definition: Contentious describes something that is likely to cause people to argue or disagree or that involves a lot of arguing. When used of a person, contentious describes someone likely or willing to argue.
example: I think it’s wise to avoid such a contentious topic at a dinner party.

definition: A tapestry is a heavy textile characterized by complicated pictorial designs and used for hangings, curtains, and upholstery. In figurative use, tapestry may refer to anything made up of different things, people, colors, etc.
example: The walls were adorned with handwoven tapestries.

definition: Egregious is a formal word used to describe things that are conspicuously bad.
example: Leaving one’s phone on during a performance is an egregious breach of theater etiquette.

definition: Palimpsest in its original use refers to writing material (such as a parchment manuscript) used one or more times after earlier writing has been erased; the underlying text is said to be “in palimpsest.” Palimpsest in extended use refers to something that has usually diverse layers or aspects apparent beneath the surface.
example: Scholars believe the motive for making palimpsests was often economic—reusing parchment was cheaper than preparing a new skin.

definition: To dissociate is to separate oneself from association or union with someone or something; in contexts relating to psychology, it has to do specifically with mentally detaching from one's physical or emotional experiences. In chemistry, dissociate means "to separate a chemical compound into its constituent parts especially through the application of heat or a solvent."
example: The director has tried to dissociate herself from her earlier films.

definition: Petulant describes a person who is angry and annoyed, or an attitude or behavior showing the emotions of such a person.
example: I didn't appreciate being accused of acting like a petulant toddler.

definition: A doppelgänger is someone who looks very much like another person. In literary use, doppelgänger refers to a ghost that closely resembles a living person.
example: I saw your doppelgänger at the movies yesterday and almost waved hello before I realized they weren’t you.

definition: To quibble is to argue or complain about small, unimportant things. Quibble can also mean "to evade the point of an argument by making trivial or frivolous objections."
example: Why are you quibbling over such a small amount of money?

definition: Facile is a formal adjective that is used disapprovingly to describe something that is too simple, or that doesn’t show enough thought or effort. Facile can also be used for something done or achieved in a way that is considered too easy or that is easily accomplished or attained. It is sometimes used approvingly, however, for someone or something that works, moves, or performs well and very easily.
example: This problem requires more than just a facile solution.

definition: Brouhaha is a synonym of both uproar and hubbub that refers to great excitement or concern about something.
example: A brouhaha erupted over the bill, even though the opposing party stood to gain just as much from its passage.

definition: To embellish something is to make it more appealing or attractive with fanciful or decorative details.
example: The gift shop had cowboy shirts and hats embellished with beads and stitching.

definition: Sui generis is a formal adjective used to describe someone or something in a class or group of its own, or in other words, unlike anyone or anything else.
example: As a scholar, she is sui generis, head and shoulders above everyone else in her field.

definition: A panacea is something that is regarded as a cure-all—that is, something that will make everything about a situation better.
example: The new program should help with the city’s housing crisis, but it’s no panacea.

definition: Like sluggish and groggy, logy describes a person who is not able to think or move normally because of being tired, sick, etc., or something that moves slowly and ploddingly.
example: The heavy meal left me feeling logy and in need of a nap.

definition: When you jettison something, you get rid of it either because it is not needed or because it is impeding your progress or otherwise weighing you down.
example: Now that the purchase of the building has been finalized, we'll revamp what we want to keep and jettison the rest.

definition: Hubris is a formal and literary word that refers to a great or foolish amount of pride or confidence.
example: The project's failure was predictable, given the inexperience and unbridled hubris of those leading the effort.

definition: Utmost describes something that is the greatest or highest in degree, number, or amount.
example: The safety of employees is of utmost importance.

definition: To devise is to invent or plan something that is difficult or complicated in some way.
example: The siblings devised a plan to clean the house from top to bottom with hopes of getting their parents to let them go to the concert.

definition: Meritorious is a formal adjective used to describe something that is deserving of honor, praise, or esteem.
example: She was honored for her meritorious service to the city.

definition: Fugitive refers to a person who runs away to avoid being captured or arrested.
example: The FBI regularly updates and circulates its list of most wanted fugitives, and asks communities where they might be seen to be careful and on the lookout.

definition: Abject usually describes things that are extremely bad or severe. It can also describe something that feels or shows shame, or someone lacking courage or strength.
example: Happily, their attempts to derail the project ended in abject failure.

definition: To tantalize someone is to cause them to feel interest or excitement about something that is very attractive, appealing, etc.
example: She was tantalized by the prospect of a big promotion.

definition: A nuance is a very small difference in something, such as color, tone, meaning, etc.
example: Amy’s musical ear makes it easy for her to detect the subtle nuances in sampled music.

definition: Contrite is a formal adjective used to describe someone who feels regret for their bad behavior, or something, such as an apology, that shows such regret.
example: Although the mayor appeared contrite about the most recent scandal plaguing city hall, many constituents remained unpersuaded.

definition: Impunity, usually used in the phrase "with impunity," refers to exemption or freedom from punishment, harm, or loss.
example: They mistakenly believe that they can break the camp's rules with impunity.

definition: To rescind something, such as a law, contract, agreement, etc., is to end it officially. Rescind can also mean “to take back; to cancel.”
example: Given the appeal court’s recent decision, it is likely that the law will be rescinded.

definition: Boffo is an informal word that describes things that are extremely good or successful.
example: The most recent film in the long-running franchise has done boffo business at the box office, a testament to the series’ enduring popularity.

definition: A simulacrum is a superficial likeness of something, usually as an imitation, copy, or representation. The plural of simulacrum is either simulacrums or simulacra.
example: The surprise still succeeded, thanks to the simulacrum of confusion expressed by two guests when they were spotted before the big moment.

definition: Something described as exemplary is extremely good and deserves to be admired and copied.
example: Our research team was awarded for our exemplary work on the project.

definition: To procrastinate is to be slow or late about doing something that should be done, or about doing or attending to things in general.
example: Tickets to the event are selling swiftly, so don't procrastinate—buy yours today.

definition: Antic refers to an attention-drawing, often wildly playful or funny act or action. It is usually used in its plural form, and is often used disapprovingly.
example: It wasn't clear which students were ultimately responsible for the antics that unfolded in the cafeteria that day.

definition: A cantankerous person is often angry and annoyed, and a cantankerous animal or thing is difficult or irritating to deal with.
example: Although the former postman was regarded by some townspeople as a scowling, cantankerous old coot, he was beloved by neighborhood children, to whom he would regularly hand out butterscotch candies from his front stoop with a twinkle in his eye.

definition: Yankee can refer broadly to anyone born or living in the U.S., more narrowly to only those in the northern U.S., or even more narrowly to only those in the states of New England. The broadest use is especially common outside the U.S.
example: It took the children some time to adjust to being the only Southerners in a classroom full of Yankees.

definition: Desultory is a formal word used to describe something that lacks a plan or purpose, or that occurs without regularity. It can also describe something unconnected to a main subject, or something that is disappointing in progress, performance, or quality.
example: After graduation, I moved from job to job in a more or less desultory manner before finding work I liked.

definition: To galumph is to move in a loud and clumsy way.
example: I could hear them galumphing around in the attic in search of old family photo albums.

definition: Someone described as verbose tends to use many words to convey their point. Verbose can also describe something, such as a speech, that contains more words than necessary.
example: The article documenting their meeting presented an odd exchange between a verbose questioner and a laconic interviewee.

definition: To expunge something is to remove it completely, whether by obliterating it, striking it out, or marking it for deletion. Expunge is most commonly applied in cases in which documentation of something is removed from an official record.
example: Due to an error, the charges were expunged from their record.

definition: Impetus refers to a force or impulse that causes something (such as a process or activity) to be done or to become more active. It is often used with for and sometimes with to.
example: Her work provided the major impetus behind the movement.

definition: Restive can describe a person or group feeling impatience or uneasiness, or it can describe someone who is stubbornly resistant to control.
example: The audience grew increasingly restive as the speaker droned on and on.

definition: To oblige a person or entity to do something is to require or force them to do it, either because of a law or rule, or because it is necessary. To simply oblige someone is to do them a favor.
example: The law obliges the government to release certain documents to the public.

definition: Sumptuous is used to describe things that are very expensive, rich, luxurious, or magnificent.
example: The celebratory meal was a sumptuous feast of dishes from our host’s homeland.

definition: Flotsam refers to the floating pieces that remain after a shipwreck, or more broadly to any floating debris or wreckage. It is also used figuratively to refer to miscellaneous or unimportant material, often in the phrase "flotsam and jetsam."
example: Driftwood and other flotsam washed onto the beach.

definition: Noisome is a formal and literary word used to describe things that are very unpleasant or disgusting; it is used especially to describe offensive smells. Noisome can also mean “highly obnoxious or objectionable” as in “we were put off by their noisome habits.”
example: The noisome odor of a trash can in the alley was so strong that even diners seated inside the adjacent restaurant complained to staff.

definition: Wherewithal refers to the means, skills, resources, or money that is needed to get or do something.
example: The company does not have the financial wherewithal to expand into other markets at this time.

definition: If you are bemused by something, you are confused or bewildered by it, and often also somewhat amused.
example: The contestant seemed somewhat bemused by the question, but gave the correct answer.

definition: A litmus test is something (such as an opinion about a political or moral issue) that is used to make a judgment about whether someone or something is acceptable.
example: At our family’s Thanksgiving dinner, the litmus test for good mac and cheese is whether or not it is baked.

definition: Convivial means "relating to, occupied with, or fond of feasting, drinking, and good company."
example: A convivial atmosphere filled the gallery, with good food in abundance, and wine and conversation both flowing freely.

definition: Emancipation refers to the act of freeing someone from the restraint, control, or power of another. It is used especially for the act of freeing someone from slavery.
example: Jomo Kenyatta played a key role in the emancipation of Kenya from European rule in the 1960s and became the first president of the newly independent nation.

definition: To jeopardize something or someone is to put them at risk or in danger.
example: The wrong decision could seriously jeopardize the success of the project.

definition: An apologia is a defense especially of one's opinions, position, or actions.
example: The opinion piece reads like an apologia for the industry's reckless behavior.

definition: Someone described as garrulous is very talkative. When garrulous is used to describe a piece of language (such as a speech), it means “containing many and often too many words; wordy.”
example: One of the dinner party guests was a garrulous poet whose stories kept most of us in stitches.

definition: Progeny refers to the child or descendant of a particular parent or family. Progeny can also refer to the offspring of an animal or plant, or broadly to something that is the product of something else. The plural of progeny is progeny.
example: Many Americans are the progeny of immigrants.

definition: Vexillology is the study of flags.
example: An expert in vexillology, Cynthia has an impressive collection of flags displayed in her home.

definition: Rambunctious describes someone or something showing uncontrolled exuberance.
example: On my first day of student teaching, I was tasked with managing a class of rambunctious youngsters.

definition: To impute something, such as a motive, act, or emotion, to a person or thing is to assert that the person or thing is guilty of that motive, act, emotion, etc.
example: It is shocking that they would impute such awful motives to me.

definition: Debilitating is a formal word used to describe things that seriously impair strength or the ability to function.
example: She suffers from debilitating migraines.

definition: Minutia refers to a small or minor detail. It is usually used in its plural form minutiae.
example: Unaccustomed to legalese, I was bewildered by the contract's minutiae.

definition: An eloquent speaker or writer expresses ideas forcefully and fluently; an eloquent speech or piece of writing likewise expresses ideas in such a way. Eloquent can also describe something that is vividly or movingly expressive.
example: She received high marks for her eloquent essay about gardening with her grandmother.

definition: Cataract refers to a clouding of the lens of the eye, or of its surrounding transparent membrane, that obstructs the passage of light. Cataract is also used, often in literature, to refer to a waterfall, steep rapids in a river, or to a downpour or flood.
example: Cataracts are common but can be corrected with surgery.

definition: Abstruse is a formal word used to describe something that is hard to understand.
example: I avoided taking this class in past semesters because the subject matter is so abstruse, but the professor does a good job explaining the concepts as clearly as possible.

definition: Festoon usually means "to cover or decorate (something) with many small objects, pieces of paper, etc.," or "to appear here and there on the surface of." It can also mean "to hang decorative chains or strips on."
example: Tiny wildflowers festooned the meadow.

definition: Sea change refers to a big and sudden change or transformation.
example: The early 2000s witnessed a sea change in public opinion about smoking in public places.

definition: Bogus is an informal word used to describe something that is not real or genuine, making it a synonym of such words as fake, false, and counterfeit.
example: We were disappointed to find out that the purses we bought were bogus.

definition: Tutelage is a formal word that refers to the instruction or guidance especially of an individual student by a teacher. Tutelage may also refer to an act or process of serving as guardian or protector.
example: Under the tutelage of his high school swim coach, Luis has greatly improved his times at meets.

definition: Something described as Herculean (often uncapitalized as herculean) is characterized by extraordinary power, extent, intensity, or difficulty.
example: Although starting a garden sounded fun in theory, the constant weeding and pest control turned it into a herculean task.

definition: Proscribe is a formal word meaning “to condemn or forbid something as harmful or unlawful.” More broadly, it can mean simply “to not allow something.”
example: The town has passed an ordinance that proscribes the ownership of snakes and other exotic pets.

definition: Opportune describes something that is suitable or convenient for a particular situation, or that is done or happening at an appropriate time.
example: They chose an opportune time to invest in real estate.

definition: Gust refers to a sudden strong wind. It is also used figuratively for a sudden outburst of something, such as a feeling.
example: Today’s weather will be windy, with gusts of up to 40 miles per hour.

definition: Nascent is a formal word used to describe something that is just beginning to exist, or in other words, is recently formed or developed.
example: The actress is now focused on her nascent singing career.

definition: A fiasco is a complete failure or disaster.
example: The entire fiasco could have been avoided if they'd simply followed the instructions.

definition: Interminable describes things that have or seem to have no end, especially because they continue for a very long time.
example: The family played games to pass the time during the interminable wait for their delayed flight.

definition: Something, such as a plaque, statue, or parade, is said to commemorate an event, person, etc. when it serves as a memorial; it exists or is done in order to recall the event or person. A person or group commemorates an event, person, etc. by doing something special in order to remember and honor that event or person.
example: The plaque commemorates the battle that took place here 200 years ago.

definition: Dyspeptic is a formal and old-fashioned word used to describe someone who is bad-tempered (in other words, easily annoyed or angered), or something that shows or is characteristic of a bad temper. The noun form of dyspeptic is dyspepsia.
example: The comedian’s shtick of delivering dyspeptic rants on the daily annoyances of modern life was enormously popular.

definition: Limn is a formal verb most often used especially in literary contexts to mean "to describe or portray," as in "a novel that limns the life of 1930s coastal Louisiana." It can also mean "to outline in clear sharp detail," as in "a tree limned by moonlight," and "to draw or paint on a surface," as in "limning a portrait."
example: The documentary limns the community's decades-long transformation.

definition: A bastion is a place or system in which something (such as an idea) is protected and continues to survive.
example: The restaurant is a bastion of the region’s ancient culinary traditions.

definition: Someone may be described as voluble if they are talking a lot in a rapid, energetic way.
example: Bri knew something was bothering her normally voluble friend when he was reluctant to talk about his day.

definition: Hapless means "having no luck." It's a synonym of unfortunate.
example: The documentary follows a hapless victim of false allegations.

definition: Chagrin refers to a feeling of frustration or annoyance caused by failure or disappointment.
example: I decided to take a gap year to the chagrin of my parents.

definition: Antithetical typically describes something that is in direct and unambiguous opposition to another thing. It is often used with to.
example: The district's new policy is fundamentally antithetical to the school's values.

definition: A talisman is an object (such as a ring or stone) that is believed to have magic powers and to cause good things to happen to the person who has it.
example: In ancient times, the gemstone was worn as a talisman to ward off evil.

definition: Mercurial is usually used to describe someone whose mood changes quickly and unpredictably. It can also describe something that changes frequently, such as weather, or something that is lively and quick, such as someone’s wit.
example: The director had some concerns about working with the play’s lead, an actor with a reputation for having a mercurial temperament on set.

definition: Junket refers to a trip that is paid for by someone else, such as a promotional trip made at another's expense, or an official's trip made at public expense.
example: The cast of the widely-acclaimed movie is making press junkets to major cities.

definition: Impervious describes that which does not allow something (such as water or light) to enter or pass through. It is also used formally to mean “not bothered or affected by something.” Both senses of impervious are usually used with to.
example: The material is impervious to water.

definition: Scuttlebutt refers to rumor or gossip—in other words, talk or stories about someone or something that may not be true.
example: According to the scuttlebutt in the financial markets, the company will be downsizing soon.

definition: Something described as apotropaic is designed or intended to avert evil.
example: The etchings are believed to be associated with ancient apotropaic rituals.

definition: Something that festers becomes worse as time passes. Fester can also mean, in the context of wounds, sores, etc., “to become painful and infected.”
example: We should deal with these problems now instead of allowing them to fester.

definition: Darling can refer to a dearly loved person or to someone who is liked very much by a person or group. It can also mean “a kind and helpful person” as in, “Be a darling and carry this inside for me, would you?”
example: Our baby grandchild is just the sweetest little darling.

definition: Uncanny is typically used to describe something that is strange or unusual in a way that is surprising or difficult to understand. It can also describe something that seems to have a supernatural character or origin.
example: The child has an uncanny ability to recognize streets and locations she's seen only once or twice before.

definition: To gloss a word or phrase is to provide its meaning, or in other words, to explain or define it.
example: Many unfamiliar terms are glossed in the book’s introduction.

definition: Modicum is a formal word that means “a small amount.” It is almost always used with of.
example: The band enjoyed a modicum of success in the early 2010s before becoming an international sensation.

definition: Bumptious describes people who are rudely and often noisily confident or over-assertive. It can also be applied to actions or behaviors that show this same attitude.
example: Our host apologized for the bumptious party guest who caused a scene before being asked to leave.

definition: To exculpate someone is to prove that they are not guilty of doing something wrong.
example: The editorial expresses confidence that the evidence will exculpate the accused.

definition: Plethora refers to a very large amount or number of something. Plethora is most often used in the phrase "a plethora of."
example: The hotel offers a plethora of amenities, including indoor and outdoor pools, a fitness center, and world-class dining.

definition: Risible is a formal word used disapprovingly to describe things that deserve to be mocked or laughed at because they are absurd or unreasonable.
example: Although the teachers derided the students’ slang as risible nonsense, the same had been said about their own generation’s lingo.

definition: To sleuth is to carefully or methodically search for information, or to act as a detective.
example: We spent hours at the flea market sleuthing for 19th century paintings.

definition: A ziggurat is an ancient Mesopotamian temple consisting of a pyramidal structure built in successive stages with outside staircases and a shrine at the top. The word ziggurat is also sometimes used for a similarly shaped structure.
example: Ancient ziggurats were always built with a core of mud brick and an exterior covered with baked brick. They had no internal chambers and were usually square or rectangular.

definition: Something described as convoluted is very complicated and difficult to understand, or has many curves and turns.
example: The speaker’s argument was so convoluted that most of the audience had trouble determining whether they were for or against the new policy.

definition: Insouciance is a formal word that refers to a feeling of carefree unconcern. It can also be understood as a word for the relaxed and calm state of a person who is not worried about anything.
example: The young actor charmed interviewers with his easy smile and devil-may-care insouciance.

definition: Furtive describes something that is done in a quiet and secret way to avoid being noticed. It can also mean "expressive of stealth" or "sly" (as in "a furtive look"), or "obtained underhandedly" (as in "furtive gains").
example: We exchanged furtive smiles across the table, carefully not to attract the teacher's attention.

definition: Alacrity refers to a quick and cheerful readiness to do something.
example: She accepted the invitation to go on the trip with an alacrity that surprised her parents, who had assumed she wouldn’t be interested.

definition: Decimate can mean both “to destroy a large number of (plants, animals, people, etc.)” or “to severely damage or destroy a large part of (something).”
example: The bay’s lobsters have been decimated by disease.

definition: Someone described as nonchalant is relaxed and calm, either because they do not care about something or because they are not worried about something. Nonchalant can also be used to describe something, such as demeanor or behavior, that expresses such relaxed, calm unconcern.
example: The team showed a somewhat nonchalant attitude at the beginning of the season, but they became more serious once the championship was within reach.

definition: Travail is a formal word, usually used in plural, that refers to a difficult experience or situation.
example: The book describes the political travails of the governor during her first year in office.

definition: Ostensible is used to describe something that seems or is said to be true or real, but is possibly not true or real. In other words, it is plausible rather than demonstrably true or real.
example: The ostensible purpose of a filibuster is to extend debate, but in reality it is used to delay or prevent action.

definition: Slough is a formal verb used for the action of getting rid of something unwanted. It is usually used with off. Slough can also mean "to lose a dead layer of (skin)" or "to become shed or cast off."
example: The editorial urges the mayor not to slough off responsibility for the errors in the report.

definition: Liaison refers to a person who helps organizations or groups work together and provide information to each other, or to a relationship that allows such interactions. Liaison can also refer to an illicit sexual relationship.
example: The new position involves acting as a liaison between the police department and city schools.

definition: Bodacious is used as an informal synonym of remarkable and noteworthy, as well as sexy and voluptuous. In some dialects of the Southern and Midland US, bodacious is used by its oldest meaning: "outright, unmistakable."
example: The bodacious decor of the boutique hotel is intended to appeal to the young and the hip.

definition: In Christian theology, Resurrection (typically capitalized in this use) refers to the event in which Jesus Christ returned to life after his death. In general contexts, resurrection refers to the act of causing something that had ended or been forgotten or lost to exist again, to be used again, etc.
example: Church members look forward to celebrating the Resurrection every Easter.

definition: Someone described as fastidious is extremely or overly careful about how they do something. Fastidious may also describe someone who is difficult to please, or someone who always wants to be clean, neat, etc.
example: Our parents taught us to be fastidious in keeping our rooms clean, making sure to dust every surface and sweep out every corner.

definition: To collaborate is to work with another person or group in order to do or achieve something. Collaborate can also be used disapprovingly to mean "to cooperate with or willingly assist an enemy of one's country and especially an enemy who occupies it during a war."
example: Several research teams from various countries collaborated closely on the project.

definition: Uncouth describes things, such as language or behavior, that are impolite or socially unacceptable. A person may also be described as uncouth if they are behaving in a rude way.
example: Stacy realized it would be uncouth to show up to the party without a gift, so she picked up a bottle of wine on the way.

definition: Adversity refers to a difficult situation or condition, or to a state of serious or continued difficulty or misfortune.
example: The soldiers were honored for acting with courage in the face of adversity.

definition: Someone described as pugnacious shows a readiness or desire to fight or argue.
example: There's one pugnacious member on the committee who won't agree to anything.

definition: Druthers is an informal word that refers to the power or opportunity to choose—in other words, free choice. It is used especially in the phrase if one had one's druthers.
example: If I had my druthers, I would travel all the time.

definition: To reminisce is to talk, think, or write about things that happened in the past.
example: After the official reunion dinner, the old friends gathered at a pub to reminisce about their high school days, now long past.

definition: Gustatory describes things that are related to or associated with eating or the sense of taste.
example: The deli has been widely praised for its astonishing variety of gustatory delights.

definition: Kitsch refers to something that appeals to popular or lowbrow taste and is often cheap or tacky. Kitsch also refers to a tacky or lowbrow quality or condition.
example: The restaurant is decorated with 1950s furniture and kitsch from old TV shows.

definition: Chary is usually used with about or of to describe someone who is cautious about doing something.
example: The director is chary about spending money.

definition: Vouchsafe is a formal and old-fashioned word meaning "to give (something) to someone as a promise or a privilege."
example: He vouchsafed the secret to only a few of his closest allies.

definition: Apparatchik is used disapprovingly to refer to a blindly devoted official, follower, or member of an organization, such as a corporation or political party.
example: This generation of graduates wants more out of life than to become establishment apparatchiks.

definition: Something described as malleable is capable of being stretched or bent into different shapes, or capable of being easily changed or influenced.
example: Let the cookie dough thaw until it becomes malleable enough to thinly roll.

definition: An impresario is a person who manages, puts on, or sponsors a performance or other entertainment, such as a concert, play, or sporting event.
example: The former heavyweight retired from the ring and later became a boxing impresario.

definition: Benign describes something that does not cause harm or damage. In medical contexts it is used to describe something that does not threaten life or health (as in "a benign tumor"). Additional meanings include "mild and pleasant" (as in "benign weather conditions") and "showing kindness and gentleness" (as in "a benign outlook").
example: The project required that we manage some inconvenient but ultimately benign conditions.

definition: Hew is commonly used with to to mean "to conform to or adhere to (something)." Hew on its own has several meanings having to do with cutting or shaping with a sharp tool, such as an ax. Both hewed and hewn are past participles of hew.
example: The senator has always hewed closely to the party line.

definition: Snark is an informal word that refers to an attitude or expression of mocking irreverence and sarcasm.
example: The stand-up comedian’s set was full of snark about current events, which had the audience rolling in the aisles.

definition: Someone or something described as effusive is expressing or showing a lot of emotion or enthusiasm.
example: Jay positively glowed as effusive compliments on the meal echoed around the table.

definition: A cynosure is a person or thing that attracts a lot of attention or interest. As a proper noun, Cynosure may refer to the North Star or its constellation Ursa Minor.
example: He was the cynosure of all eyes as he walked into the room.

definition: Penchant refers to a strong liking for something, or a strong tendency to behave in a certain way. It is usually used with for.
example: My penchant for mathematics helped me become an engineer.

definition: Untoward is a formal word that describes something that is improper or inappropriate, or that is adverse or unfavorable.
example: The medication is safe and effective, with no known untoward side effects.

definition: To elucidate something is to make it clear or easy to understand.
example: The writer elucidates complex medical findings for a general audience.

definition: Derelict is a formal word that describes something that is no longer cared for or used by anyone. It can also describe someone who is negligent or who fails to do what needs to be done.
example: The kids made sure to stay away from the spooky derelict houses in the neighborhood on Halloween.

definition: Archetype refers to someone or something that is seen to be a perfect example. It is also a word for the original pattern or model of which all things of the same type are representations or copies.
example: The college’s most popular philosophy professor is the archetype of the preoccupied academic, complete with the messy desk, disheveled hair, and brilliant theories.

definition: Something described as flippant, such as behavior or a comment, is lacking in proper respect or seriousness.
example: The celebrity made a flippant remark when questioned about the scandal.

definition: A hobbit is a member of a fictitious peaceful and friendly race of small humanlike creatures that dwell underground.
example: The story was filled with all sorts of imaginary people, including hobbits.

definition: To garble something, such as a word, name, message, etc., is to cause it to be unclear or distorted. This type of garbling can be the result of an accident, ignorance, or a transmission error. Garble can also mean "to so alter or distort as to create a wrong impression or change the meaning."
example: I was so nervous I garbled their names.

definition: De rigueur is a formal adjective that describes things that are necessary if you want to be fashionable, popular, socially acceptable, etc.—in other words, things required by fashion, etiquette, or custom.
example: Dark sunglasses are de rigueur these days among fashionistas.

definition: Neologism can refer either to a new word or expression or to a new meaning of an existing word.
example: I love seeing all the slangy neologisms that pop up on social media every year.

definition: To permeate is to pass or spread through something.
example: The scent of lilacs permeated the room.

definition: Vernal is a formal adjective that describes something that relates to or occurs in the spring.
example: It is such a relief after a long, cold winter to see the trees and flowers in their glorious vernal bloom.

definition: A juggernaut is something (such as a force, campaign, or movement) that is extremely large and powerful and cannot be stopped.
example: The team is a juggernaut this year, winning more games than any team before it has.

definition: To admonish someone is to express warning or disapproval towards them, or to urge them to do something.
example: We were admonished for arriving late to the meeting.

definition: A limerick is a humorous rhyming poem of five lines.
example: My limerick received a prize for the funniest poem at the open mic night.

definition: Rife usually describes things that are very common and often—though not always—bad or unpleasant. Rife is also commonly used in the phrase “rife with” to mean “copiously supplied” or “having a large amount of; full of.” Unlike most adjectives, rife is not used before a noun.
example: Speculation about who would be sent to the new office had been rife for weeks.

definition: A stratagem is a trick or plan for deceiving an enemy or for achieving a goal.
example: They devised various stratagems to get the cat into the carrier, but the feisty feline was wise to them all.

definition: To bamboozle someone is to deceive, trick, or confuse them.
example: The salesperson bamboozled us into getting a more expensive item than we had planned to buy.

definition: Curfew refers to a law or order that requires people to be indoors after a certain time at night, as well as to the period of time when such an order or law is in effect. Chiefly in the United States, curfew is also used to refer to the time set by a parent or caregiver at which a child has to be back home after going out.
example: No one is allowed on the streets during the curfew.

definition: Something described as multifarious has great diversity or variety, or is made up of many and various kinds of things. Multifarious is a formal word and a synonym of diverse.
example: He participated in multifarious activities throughout college.

definition: Quark is a word used in physics to refer to any one of several types of very small particles that make up matter.
example: Quarks, which combine together to form protons and neutrons, come in six types, or flavors: up, down, charm, strange, top, and bottom.

definition: Imperturbable describes someone or something marked by extreme calm; such a person or thing is very hard to disturb or upset.
example: The imperturbable captain did not panic when the boat sailed into the path of a violent storm.

definition: Wend is a literary word that means “to move slowly from one place to another usually by a winding or indirect course”; wending is traveling or proceeding on one’s way in such a manner.
example: Hikers wend along the marked trails to the top of the mountain, which provides a panoramic view of the area towns.

definition: Gregarious is used to describe someone who enjoys the company of other people.
example: Justin’s gregarious personality made it easy for him to get to know people at the networking event.

definition: An emollient is something, such as a lotion, that softens or soothes.
example: She keeps a number of oils in the bathroom—argan, almond, and coconut—to use as emollients.

definition: To career is to go at top speed especially in a headlong manner.
example: The tourists gripped their seats and exchanged anxious looks as the bus careered along the narrow roads.

definition: Askew means “not straight” or “at an angle,” and can be used as both an adjective and an adverb.
example: The picture on the cabin wall was slightly askew.

definition: Schadenfreude refers to a feeling of enjoyment that comes from seeing or hearing about the troubles of other people.
example: Schadenfreude was felt by many viewers when the arrogant contestant was voted off the show.

definition: Draconian describes something (often a law, policy, restriction, etc.) that is very severe or cruel.
example: The editorial criticizes the draconian measures being taken by city hall to rein in spending.

definition: Transpire is a formal verb that means “to happen,” or in other words “to take place or occur.” It can also mean “to come to light” or “to become known,” as in “It transpired that they had met previously.” In botany, to transpire is to give off or exude watery vapor especially from the surfaces of leaves.
example: The monument will ensure that posterity will not soon forget the historic events that transpired on that day.

definition: A factoid is a brief and usually unimportant or trivial fact. Factoid may also refer to an invented fact believed to be true because it appears in print.
example: The book is really just a collection of interesting factoids.

definition: Something described as cryptic has or seems to have a hidden meaning, or is difficult to understand.
example: The singer posted a cryptic message on her social media accounts, and fans raced to decipher it.

definition: To doff a hat or other piece of clothing is to take it off.
example: They doffed their coats when they came inside the house.

definition: An ignoramus is an utterly ignorant or stupid person.
example: I can't believe they let an ignoramus like that run the company.

definition: Superfluous is a formal word used to describe things that exceed what is necessary or sufficient, or that are simply not needed.
example: Further discussion seems superfluous, given the thorough conversation we just had.

definition: Quip can refer to a clever, usually taunting remark, or to a witty or funny observation or response usually made on the spur of the moment.
example: They traded quips over a beer and laughed themselves silly.

definition: To tousle something is to dishevel it—that is, to make it untidy or unkempt. Tousle is usually, though not always, used specifically when a person’s hair is being so treated.
example: Vic stood in front of the mirror and tousled his hair, trying to get a cool, disheveled look.

definition: Someone or something described as astute has or shows an ability to notice and understand things clearly. In other words, they are mentally sharp or clever. Astute can also describe someone who is crafty or wily.
example: They made some astute observations about the movie industry.

definition: Jabberwocky refers to meaningless speech or writing.
example: When the character gets angry or flustered, she talks in a sort of agitated jabberwocky that is really quite comical.

definition: To flounder is to struggle, whether that struggle is about moving or obtaining footing (as in “horses floundering through deep snow”) or about knowing what to do or say.
example: Caught off-guard by the reporter’s question, the mayor floundered for a few moments before remembering the talking points he had rehearsed.

definition: Obtuse is a formal word that describes someone who is not able to think clearly or to understand what is obvious or simple. It can also suggest a refusal to see something apparent to others, or a willful ignorance of or insensitivity to the real facts of a situation. Obtuse can also describe something that is difficult to understand because it is unclear or imprecise.
example: They were too obtuse to take a hint.

definition: Chutzpah is audacious boldness often paired with reckless self-confidence. Someone with chutzpah dares to do or say things that seem shocking to others.
example:
It took a lot of chutzpah to stand up to her boss the way she did.

1. list text here

definition: To pertain to someone or something is to relate, refer, or have a connection to that person or thing.
example: That law pertains only to people who live in this state.

definition: A non sequitur is a statement that either does not logically follow from, or is not clearly related to, what was previously said.
example: We were talking about the new restaurant when she threw in some non sequitur about her dog.

definition: Livid means "very angry, enraged, or furious." It may also describe things having a dark purplish or reddish color.
example: The teen's parents were livid when they discovered she had lied about her whereabouts.

definition: A billet-doux is a love letter. The word's plural is billets-doux.
example: Since their relationship was long-distance, the couple thought it would be cute to send each other billets-doux on their anniversary.

definition: Someone or something described as gallant is very courageous and brave. Gallant is also sometimes used to mean “large and impressive” (as in “a gallant ship”), or to describe someone who has or shows politeness and respect for women.
example: Though they failed to reach the summit, the mountaineering team made a gallant attempt.

definition: Hagiography is biography that idealizes or idolizes a person and their life.
example: The book gives a good idea of his virtues without resorting to hagiography.

definition: To ruminate is to think carefully and deeply about something.
example: We ruminated over the implications of our decision.

definition: A vestige is a trace, mark, or visible sign left by something lost or vanished.
example: The ruins here are the last vestiges of the Roman occupation in this part of Britain.

definition: Someone described as ecstatic is very happy or excited; the person feels or shows ecstasy—that is, rapturous delight.
example: Greta and Sam were ecstatic when their daughter called to tell them that they were soon going to be grandparents.

definition: To finesse something is to bring it about, direct it, or manage it by skillful maneuvering.
example: We managed to finesse a favorable deal on some Beatles LPs at the flea market through subtle bargaining.

definition: A malapropism is an amusing error that occurs when a person mistakenly uses a word that sounds like another word but that has a very different meaning.
example: "It's lovely to see all of you on this suspicious occasion," our host said. A flurry of snickers were heard in reply; the malapropism (she had of course meant to call it an "auspicious" occasion) was characteristic.

definition: To ad-lib something, such as a performance or part of a performance, is to improvise it—that is, to make up words or music instead of saying, singing, or playing something that has been planned.
example: The actor forgot his lines, so he ad-libbed.

definition: Canard refers to a false report or story, or to a belief or rumor that isn't true. It can also refer to a kind of airplane as well as to a kind of small airfoil.
example: The book unfortunately repeats some of history's oldest canards.

definition: Someone described as zaftig has a full, rounded figure, or in other words is pleasingly plump.
example: Portraits of zaftig models are exhibited in the artist's collection.

definition: Sarcophagus refers to a coffin, and specifically a stone coffin.
example: The crypt under the abbey church contains the sarcophagus of the monastery's founding abbot.

definition: To presage something is to give or be a sign that it will happen in the future. Presage is a formal synonym of foreshadow, foretell, and predict.
example: The sudden gloom and ominous dark clouds clearly presaged a nasty storm.

definition: Disputatious is a formal word used to describe someone who often disagrees and argues with other people (in other words, someone inclined to dispute). It can also describe something marked or characterized by arguments or controversies, or something that provokes debate or controversy.
example: The podcast is hosted by a disputatious pair whose sparring has drawn legions of listeners.

definition: To encroach is to gradually move or go into an area that is beyond the usual or desired limits, or to gradually take or begin to use or affect something that belongs to, or is being used by, someone else. Encroach is often followed by on or upon.
example: Conflicts between people and bears increase as humans continue to encroach on bear territory.

definition: An audition is a short performance to show the talents of someone (such as an actor or a musician) who is being considered for a role in a play, a position in an orchestra, etc.
example: Auditions will be held next week for the spring musical.

definition: Facetious is used to describe something, such as a remark or behavior, that is meant to be humorous or funny but is sometimes instead annoying, silly, or improper. It can also be used to describe someone who is joking, often implying that they are doing so inappropriately.
example: The emcee delivered several facetious quips throughout the night that the audience found in poor taste.

definition: Sward is a literary word that refers to an area of land covered with grass.
example: The hikers emerged from the forest to find a green sward dotted with yellow and purple flowers stretching out before them.

definition: To edify someone is to teach them in a way that improves their mind or character.
example: The commencement speaker hoped that her words would edify the graduates, and give them hope and encouragement.

definition: If something—such as a path, route, or journey—is described as circuitous, it is not straight, short, and direct, but rather takes a circular or winding course. Circuitous can also describe speech or writing that is not said or done simply or clearly.
example: He took a circuitous route to town, stopping at several of his favorite shops even though it added minutes and miles to his trip.

definition: Nomenclature is a formal word that refers to a system of names that is used in specialized fields and especially in science. Nomenclature is also used more broadly as a synonym of name and designation.
example: It took Faith, a trained herpetologist, a while to become familiar with the nomenclature used at the entomology conference.

definition: Divers is an adjective meaning "numbering more than one."
example: The tri-county fair offers divers amusements for the whole family.

definition: Wanderlust refers to a strong desire to travel.
example: During their final semester at college, the two friends were both filled with an insatiable wanderlust and began planning a journey to Patagonia together.

definition: To opine is to express an opinion about something.
example: Many people opine that social media platforms should be better regulated.

definition: A gourmand is a person who loves and appreciates good food and drink. Gourmand can also refer to someone who enjoys eating and drinking to excess.
example: He was a gourmand who retired to New Orleans to live close to the cuisine he loved best.

definition: Inimitable describes someone or something that is impossible to copy or imitate.
example: Courtnay delivered the speech in her own inimitable style.

definition: Virtuoso is used broadly to refer to a person who does something very skillfully, and is often used specifically to refer to a very skillful musician.
example: He’s a real virtuoso in the kitchen, whipping up gourmet dishes for his family not just on holidays but on regular weeknights.

definition: Something described as minuscule is very small. Minuscule can also mean "written in, or in the size or style of, lowercase letters," in which case it can be contrasted with majuscular.
example: The number of bugs in the latest version of the video game is minuscule compared to the number that surfaced in the beta version.

definition: Apprehension most often refers to the fear that something bad or unpleasant is going to happen; it’s a feeling of being worried about the future. The word can also refer to seizure by legal process.
example: There is growing apprehension that next quarter’s profits will be lower than expected.

definition: To parlay something is to use or develop it in order to get something else of greater value. Parlay is often used with the word into.
example: He hoped to parlay his basketball skills into a college scholarship.

definition: Something is considered hackneyed when it is not interesting, funny, etc., because of being used too often; in other words, it's neither fresh nor original.
example: The new crime drama's characters are shallow stereotypes who engage one another in hackneyed dialogue.

definition: A deus ex machina is a character or thing that suddenly enters the story in a novel, play, movie, etc., and solves a problem that had previously seemed impossible to solve.
example: The introduction of a new love interest in the final act was the perfect deus ex machina for the main character's happy ending.

definition: Secular describes things that are not spiritual; that is, they relate more to the physical world than the spiritual world. The word also carries the closely related meaning of "not religious."
example: Each year, Ian directed his charitable giving toward secular concerns like affordable housing and arts programming for teens.

definition: A leitmotif is a dominant recurring theme—something (such as a melody, an idea, or a phrase) repeated many times throughout a book, story, opera, etc.
example: The overcoming of obstacles and a love of theater are the two leitmotifs of her autobiography.

definition: To cozen someone is to deceive, win over, or induce them to do something by coaxing or trickery.
example: The organization cozened scores of people by persuading them to participate in a fraudulent investment scheme.

definition: Something, such as a position, excuse, or situation, that is described as untenable cannot be defended against attack or criticism.
example: The scientists considered their colleague's theory to be bold but ultimately untenable.

definition: Excursion refers to a trip, and especially to a short one made for pleasure. Excursion is also often used figuratively to refer to a deviation from a direct, definite, or proper course, and often in particular to a digression.
example: Some of Maya’s most cherished childhood memories are of fishing excursions with her grandpa.

definition: Something described as gelid, such as the weather or a person’s demeanor, is literally or figuratively extremely cold or icy.
example: She decided to move down south after experiencing Chicago’s gelid winters throughout college.

definition: To beleaguer a person, business, etc. is to cause them constant or repeated trouble. Beleaguer is also sometimes used as a synonym of besiege.
example: The coach, beleaguered by the media and fans for his poor decision-making during games, has been fired.

definition: Tome is a formal word for a book, and especially a very large, thick, often scholarly book.
example: We picked up a tome on the Ghana Empire for our history project.

definition: Cerulean describes things whose blue color resembles the blue of a clear sky.
example: The painting depicts leafless trees bordering a cerulean lake.

definition: To fulminate is to complain loudly or angrily about something.
example: The editorial fulminated against the corruption in the state government that has been recently uncovered.

definition: Someone described as addlepated is mixed-up or confused. Addlepated can also be used as synonym of eccentric.
example: Some addlepated clerk confused our hotel reservation with that of another, similarly named, party.

definition: Potpourri is a mixture of dried flower petals, leaves, and spices that is used to make a room smell pleasant. When used figuratively potpourri refers to a collection of various different things.
example: Her favorite winter potpourri includes cinnamon sticks, cloves, and orange peel.

definition: To rejuvenate a person, parts of the body, etc., is to make them feel young, healthy, or energetic again. To rejuvenate something abstract, such as an economy or career, is to give it new strength or energy.
example: The hotel package includes a day at the spa to rejuvenate guests.

definition: Zeitgeist refers to the general beliefs, ideas, and spirit of a time and place.
example: The artist’s songs perfectly captured the zeitgeist of 1990s America.

definition: Someone described as urbane is notably polite, confident, or polished in manner. Urbane is also used to describe things that are fashionable and somewhat formal.
example: "When did my willful, childish cousin turn into this urbane young artist greeting the guests at her opening reception?" wondered Elena.
