definition: Linchpin, sometimes spelled lynchpin, literally refers to a locking pin inserted crosswise, as at the end of an axle or shaft. In figurative use, linchpin refers to a person or thing that serves to hold together parts or elements that exist or function as a unit; such a linchpin is often understood as the most important part of a complex situation or system.
example: Investors are betting that the new product line will be the linchpin that secures the company's place in the very competitive market in the years and decades to come.

definition: To condone something that is considered wrong is to forgive or approve it, or to allow it to continue.
example: We cannot condone that kind of behavior.

definition: Feisty describes someone who has or shows a lively aggressiveness especially in being unafraid to fight or argue. In some regions of the US, feisty may also be used as a synonym of fidgety, quarrelsome, or frisky.
example: Even her opponents admire her feisty spirit.

definition: A menorah is a candelabra with seven or nine lights that is used in Jewish worship.
example: At sundown on the first night of Hanukkah, Elliott's father helped him light the first candle on the menorah.

definition: Evergreen in its figurative uses describes something, such as a plot, that retains its freshness or interest over a long period of time, or something, such as an issue or concern, that is universally and continually relevant. In botany, evergreen describes foliage that remains green and functional through more than one growing season.
example: For their first pick of the new year, the book club chose an evergreen self-help book.

definition: To wassail is to sing carols (popular songs or ballads of religious joy) from house to house at Christmas; the verb is usually used in the phrase "go wassailing." As a noun, wassail can refer to (among other things) a hot drink that is made with wine, beer, or cider, as well as spices, sugar, and usually baked apples. Wassail is traditionally served in a large bowl especially at Christmastime.
example: Every year at Christmastime the magazine publishes a recipe for the traditional drink served to those who go wassailing and may appear at one's doorstep.

definition: Delectation is a formal word for a feeling of delight or enjoyment. It can also be used to refer to the source of such feelings.
example: The resort staff left a sampling of fine chocolate in our room for our delectation.

definition: In technical use, ambient describes things—such as air quality or light in a room—that exist or are present on all sides. Ambient is also used to describe electronic music that is quiet and relaxing, with melodies that repeat many times.
example: The chemicals must be kept at an ambient temperature of 70°F.

definition: A testimonial is a written or spoken statement in which a person says they used a product or service and liked it, or that they appreciate someone's work, skill, character, etc. Testimonial is also used as a synonym of evidence and testimony.
example: The website is full of testimonials from satisfied customers.

definition: Beatific is a formal word that describes something or someone having a blissful appearance or showing complete happiness.
example: As the pair danced, beatific smiles on their faces, the audience sat hushed and almost reverential.

definition: To requite is to give or do something in return for something that another person has given or done, or for a benefit or service that has been provided.
example: Sam was worried that the feelings she’d expressed on her date were not requited, but was relieved and overjoyed to learn that they were.

definition: A qualm is a feeling of doubt or uncertainty about whether one is doing the right thing, or whether something is right or proper. Qualm is often used in its plural form, as in “I have no qualms with that decision.”
example: Elena’s parents had no qualms about her organizing a dinner party for her three closest friends.

definition: To describe something as lexical is to say that it is related to words or vocabulary.
example: A dictionary provides lexical information—it tells you what the word "cat" means, not all there is to know about cats.

definition: An allusion is a reference to something that avoids mentioning the thing directly. Allusion may also describe the use of such a statement or the act of alluding to something.
example: The lyrics contain biblical allusions.

definition: Someone described as cavalier shows no concern for important or serious matters. Cavalier also describes attitudes, manners, etc., that show the same lack of concern.
example: The company provides regular training about the dangers of being cavalier in sharing privileged information.

definition: To venerate someone or something is to feel or show deep respect for them because they are considered great, holy, etc.
example: Her best-selling trilogy led to her becoming a writer venerated by generations of admirers.

definition: Something described as immense is very great in size, degree, or amount.
example: They inherited an immense fortune.

definition: Pastiche refers to something (such as a piece of writing, music, etc.) that imitates the style of someone or something else. It can also refer to a work that is made up of selections from multiple other works, or it can be used as a synonym of hodgepodge.
example: The director’s new murder mystery is a clever pastiche of the 1950s noir films she watched as a girl.

definition: To sublimate something—such as an impulse, desire, or feeling—is to express it in a changed form that is socially acceptable. Sublimate can also mean "to pass directly from the solid to the vapor state."
example: Nora later came to understand that she had used painting to sublimate her anger.

definition: A brogue is a low shoe, usually made of leather, that is decorated with small holes along the sides at the toe, and that usually features a wing tip.
example: Even though his brogues are scuffed and old, Dad prefers them to his new loafers.

definition: Fulgent is a formal, often poetic word used to describe something that is dazzlingly bright. It is a synonym of radiant.
example: After a long, drizzly morning, a fulgent sun finally peeked out from behind the clouds.

definition: To galvanize people is to cause them to be so excited or concerned about something that they are driven to action.
example: The council’s proposal to close the library has galvanized the town’s residents.

definition: Misbegotten describes things that are badly planned or thought out.
example: They were sent on a misbegotten diplomatic mission that was sure to fail.

definition: An ambigram is an image of a written word or phrase that is intended or able to be oriented in either of two ways for viewing or reading.
example: Angel started taking calligraphy classes to learn how to create ambigrams and other fun designs that can be read both upside down and right side up.

definition: To drub an individual or team, as in a game or contest, is to defeat them decisively.
example: Morale after the game was low: the hometown team had been drubbed by the worst team in the league.

definition: Someone or something described as hoity-toity may also be called snooty or pretentious; hoity-toity people appear to think that they are better, smarter, or more important than other people, and hoity-toity places and things seem to be made for those same people. An informal word, hoity-toity is a synonym of pompous, fancy, and highfalutin.
example: The guidance counselor emphasized that students do not need to go to a hoity-toity college to achieve success.

definition: To eschew something is to avoid it, especially because you do not think it is right, proper, or practical.
example: Their teacher was known as a Luddite because he eschewed the use of smartphones and tablets in the classroom.

definition: Someone described as complaisant is willing or eager to please other people, or is easily convinced to do what other people want.
example: Derek was a complaisant boy, always happy to oblige whenever his mother or father asked him to run an errand.

definition: A scintilla is a very small amount of something. Scintilla is usually used in negative statements, as in “not even/nary a scintilla.”
example: There wasn’t even a scintilla of evidence to support their story.

definition: Someone described as frugal is careful about spending money or using things unnecessarily. Frugal can also describe something that is simple and plain in a way that reflects such carefulness with money and resources.
example: By being frugal and limiting unnecessary purchases, the family is able to stretch its monthly budget.

definition: To obfuscate something is to make it more difficult to understand. Obfuscate can also mean “to be evasive, unclear, or confusing.”
example: The revised wording of the rule obfuscates its meaning.

definition: Victuals is a word with an old-fashioned feel that refers to food, and sometimes to both food and drink.
example: Rachel’s grandparents’ larder was full of canned tomatoes and peaches, jars of pickled beans, jugs of dandelion wine, and other time-honored victuals.

definition: A guttural sound—such as speech, laughter, or a grunt—is formed or pronounced in the throat.
example: Her friends always found her deep, guttural laugh to be highly contagious.

definition: An eddy is a current of water or air running contrary to the main current, especially as a whirlpool. In figurative use, eddy may also refer to a contrary or circular current of thought or policy.
example: The strong gusts whipped up eddies of fallen leaves.

definition: To chastise someone is to criticize them harshly for doing something wrong.
example: The waiter was chastised for forgetting the customer’s order.

definition: Someone or something described as lenient is not harsh, severe, or strict. In other words, they allow a lot of freedom and leeway, and do not punish or correct in a strong way.
example: The teacher was lenient in her grading after the holiday break.

definition: To negotiate is to discuss something formally in order to make an agreement. Negotiate can also mean, when applied to people or things in motion, "to get through, around, or over successfully."
example: The parties negotiated an agreement.

definition: Paroxysm is a formal word that refers to a sudden strong feeling or uncontrollable expression of emotion. In medical use, paroxysm refers to a sudden attack or increase of symptoms of a disease that often occurs repeatedly.
example: The comedy special sent us into paroxysms of laughter.

definition: Something described as tenacious cannot easily be stopped or pulled apart; in other words, it is firm or strong. Tenacious can also describe something—such as a myth—that continues or persists for a long time, or someone who is determined to do something.
example: Caleb was surprised by the crab’s tenacious grip.

definition: To snivel is to speak or act in a whining, sniffling, tearful, or weakly emotional manner. The word snivel may also be used to mean "to run at the nose," "to snuffle," or "to cry or whine with snuffling."
example: She was unmoved by the millionaires sniveling about their financial problems.

definition: Moot typically describes something that is no longer important or worth discussing. It can also describe something that is argued about but not possible for people to prove.
example: I think they were wrong, but the point is moot. Their decision has been made and it can't be changed now.

definition: To denigrate someone is to criticize them heavily and often unfairly. Denigrate can also mean "to make something seem less important or valuable."
example: Her essay denigrates her mentor as a person and as a teacher.

definition: Grandiloquence is a formal word that refers to the use of extravagantly colorful or pompous language often in order to sound impressive and important.
example: He was known for the flowery grandiloquence of his speeches which, his passionate delivery notwithstanding, always caused more than a few listeners to doze off.

definition: Someone described as steadfast is very devoted or loyal to a person, belief, or cause. Steadfast is also used to describe something, such as support, that remains unchanging.
example: Despite the singer’s recent change in creative direction, his true fans have remained steadfast.

definition: Cachet is used as a synonym of prestige to refer to the respect and admiration someone or something receives for being successful or important. It can also be used to refer to a characteristic feature or quality that confers such prestige.
example: His research in Antarctica gave him a certain cachet among other scientists.

definition: Someone described as raddled is in a confused or befuddled state (as from drinking). Raddled can also describe things that are broken-down or worn.
example: We were met at the door by a raddled old man who turned out to be the actor’s father, and who in his day had also been an estimable presence on the London stage.

definition: A bevy is a large group of people or things. Bevy is usually used in the singular form and accompanied by the word of.
example: The new streaming platform featured a bevy of new movies to choose from.

definition: Someone or something described as labile is readily open to change. Labile can also be used as a synonym of unstable to describe things that are readily or continually undergoing chemical, physical, or biological change or breakdown.
example: The director was known for being exacting but also labile, open to actors' interpretations of characters.

definition: An armistice is an agreement to stop fighting a war, or in other words, a truce.
example: Both sides in the conflict agreed to an armistice.

definition: To truncate something—such as a discussion or essay—is to make it shorter.
example: The interview was truncated and edited for clarity.

definition: Inchoate is a formal adjective that describes something that is not completely formed or developed yet.
example: In the podcast, the author described the process by which she took a series of inchoate vignettes and shaped them into her best-selling novel.

definition: To feign something (such as surprise, ignorance, or sleep) is to pretend to feel or be affected by it.
example: I would never feign illness just to get out of a test.

definition: Dedication refers to devotion, loyalty, or commitment to a person or cause. It can also refer to a message at the beginning of a book, song, etc., that expresses affection or gratitude for someone, or to a ceremony to mark the official completion or opening of something, such as a building.
example: It took a lot of hard work and dedication, but we managed to finish the project on time.

definition: When a song is performed a cappella, it is sung unaccompanied by instrumental music.
example: A hush fell over the audience as a voice from offstage began singing a cappella.

definition: Psephology is the scientific study of elections.
example: Brianna was excited to learn that a course on psephology on the schedule for next semester will coincide with local and state elections.

definition: Amalgamate is a formal verb meaning "to unite (two or more things) into one thing."
example: The band became famous for amalgamating different musical styles into a unique, signature sound.

definition: Something described as cursory has been done or made quickly.
example: We were disappointed that the mayor gave only a cursory glance at our report.

definition: To extricate someone or something is to free or remove that person or thing from an entanglement or difficulty, such as a trap or a difficult conversation.
example: She hasn't been able to extricate herself from her legal problems.

definition: Hatching refers to the drawing or engraving of lines close together as a method of shading, or to a pattern so created.
example: The artist uses hatching to breathe life into her comics.

definition: Hallowed describes something, such as a memorial, considered holy or blessed, or something that is highly respected and revered.
example: The church stands on hallowed ground.

definition: Syncretism refers to the combining of different forms of belief or practice.
example: As a scholar of religion, Laila is especially interested in the syncretism of Manichaeism, which was influenced by Christianity, Buddhism, and Zoroastrianism.

definition: Omniscient describes someone or something with unlimited knowledge or understanding.
example: "You'll need to tell me when you don't understand something I've explained," Maria said. "I'm not omniscient, you know."

definition: A disbursement is a payout of money from a fund that has been created for a special purpose. Disbursement can also refer to the money that is paid out.
example: The company has made large disbursements for research.

definition: To usurp something (such as power) is to take and keep it by force and without the right to do so. Usurp can also mean "to take the place of by or as if by force."
example: Some people have accused city council members of trying to usurp the mayor’s power.

definition: Categorical is a synonym of absolute and definite that describes something that is said in a very strong and clear way. It can also mean "of, relating to, or constituting a category" or "involving, according with, or considered with respect to specific categories."
example: The organization has issued a categorical denial about its involvement in the deal.

definition: Euphoria refers to a feeling of great happiness and excitement.
example: The initial euphoria following their championship victory has since subsided.

definition: To garnish food or drink is to add decorative and tasty touches to it, such as a spiral of lemon peel.
example: Aditi likes to garnish her mashed potatoes with chives and a dollop of sour cream.

definition: Palaver is an informal word that usually refers to unimportant or meaningless talk. It can also refer to misleading or deceptive speech, or to a conference or discussion. In British English the word is sometimes used as a synonym of fuss to refer to unnecessary excitement about something.
example: Enough of this palaver. We have more important things to discuss.

definition: Betwixt is a synonym of between that lends an old-fashioned feel to both speech and writing. It is sometimes used in the phrase "betwixt and between" to mean "in the middle" or "neither one thing nor the other."
example: Charley took a seat betwixt two other passengers.

definition: Intransigent is a formal word that describes a person who refuses to compromise or abandon an often extreme position or attitude. It can also describe a thing, such as a system or point of view, that shows the same kind of stubbornness.
example: Despite the mediator's best efforts, the opposing sides in the dispute remained intransigent.

definition: Defenestration is most often used to refer to a usually swift dismissal or expulsion, as from a political party or office. It is also used to refer to a throwing of a person or thing out of a window.
example: Once fancying itself something of a big tent, the group now seeks the defenestration of any local leader who isn't aligned with the current mayor's administration.

definition: Appreciable describes things that can be perceived or measured.
example: Researchers found that the temperature change made no appreciable difference in the chemical reaction.

definition: Zest refers to an enjoyably exciting quality, or to keen enjoyment itself. In culinary use, zest refers to small pieces of the peel of a lemon, lime, orange, or other citrus fruit used as flavoring.
example: His humor added zest to the presentation's admittedly dry material.

definition: Fugacious is a formal word that describes something that lasts only a short time.
example: The rock band’s early success proved fugacious; within two years its members had moved on to other careers.

definition: To exact something (such as payment or revenge) is to demand it and get it, especially by using force or threats.  Exact is also used in phrases like "exact a terrible toll" and "exact a high/heavy price" to say that something has caused a lot of suffering, loss, etc.
example: The novel's protagonist is undeterred by either time or circumstance in her effort to exact revenge.

definition: A rendition, simply put, is the act or result of rendering something. That thing may be a performance or interpretation, a depiction, or a translation. In US law, rendition refers to the surrender by a state of a fugitive to another state that is charging the fugitive with a crime.
example: Their signature meat loaf is a fine rendition of a classic recipe.

definition: Taciturn is a formal word that describes someone who tends to be quiet or who tends to speak infrequently.
example: One of the twins was taciturn and shy, while the other one was more outgoing.

definition: To ideate is to form an idea or conception of something.
example: Jocelyn used the education seminar's lunch hour to talk with other teachers and ideate new activities to use in the classroom.

definition: Verbatim is an adverb meaning "in the exact words," or in other words, "word for word."
example: The coach was quoted verbatim in the article announcing that she would retire at the end of the season.

definition: A scapegoat is a person who is unfairly blamed for something others have done.
example: The CFO was made the scapegoat for the company’s failures.

definition: Numinous is a formal, often literary, word that typically describes things that have a mysterious or spiritual quality. It can also describe something holy or something that appeals to one's aesthetic sense.
example: We were overcome by the numinous atmosphere of the catacombs.

definition: To coruscate is to give off or reflect light in bright beams or flashes. Coruscate is used as a synonym of sparkle and may also be used to mean "to be brilliant or showy in technique or style."
example: She placed a bid on a classic car from the 1950s, replete with yards of coruscating chrome.

definition: Exorbitant describes something that goes far beyond what is fair, reasonable, or expected (as by being too high, too expensive, etc.).
example: The cost of our stay was so exorbitant you would have thought that we had bought the hotel and not just spent a few nights there.

definition: Lèse-majesté (less commonly spelled lese majesty) can refer to a true crime or offense, or to something likened to a crime or offense. Most often, it’s the latter, with lèse-majesté referring—seriously or playfully—to an act of disrespect that diminishes the dignity or importance of someone or something. In the former use, lèse-majesté refers to a crime (such as treason) that is committed against a sovereign power, or to an offense that violates the dignity of a ruler as the representative of a sovereign power.
example: Their less-than-formal attire at the wedding was regarded in jest as lèse-majesté.

definition: To berate someone is to angrily scold or criticize them, often loudly and at length.
example: “Don’t berate yourself over canceling plans,” his friend told him. “Sometimes you just need to take care of yourself.”

definition: An adversary is an enemy or opponent.
example: Upon learning that its adversaries were ahead in sales, the company quickly formed a new advertising campaign.

definition: Something described as gossamer—such as a butterfly wing or a thin fabric—is very light or delicate.
example: Except for a few gossamer clouds, the sky was clear and blue.

definition: Posterity is a formal word that refers to all future generations of people. It is often, though not always, used with for or to.
example: A record of the events was preserved for posterity.

definition: To fret is to worry or be concerned.
example: I was sure we wouldn’t get there in time, but they told me not to fret.

definition: Chthonic means "of or relating to the underworld." It is used as a synonym of infernal.
example: Cleo compared entering her brother's basement bedroom to a descent into chthonic regions: it was dark and odd-smelling, and she was a little frightened of what she might find there.

definition: Tribulation, which is often used in the phrase "trials and tribulations," refers to an experience that causes suffering. It can also mean "unhappiness, pain, or suffering."
example: The new graduate knew that the journey to becoming a successful entrepreneur would come with some trials and tribulations.

definition: Feckless describes people or things that are weak or ineffective.
example: The agency’s response to the dramatic increase in air pollution was well-intentioned but ultimately feckless.

definition: An avatar is an electronic image (as in a video game) that represents, and can be manipulated by, a computer user. Avatar can also refer to the embodiment of something (such as a concept or philosophy) often in a person, or to an incarnation of a deity—especially a Hindu deity, such as Vishnu.
example: Before they started playing the game, Maeve and Sanaa customized their avatars.

definition: If something written, spoken, or otherwise communicated is described as lucid, it is very clear and easy to understand. A person described as lucid is able to think clearly. Lucid is also used to describe things that are luminous, or that are visually transparent.
example: The film conveyed a lucid message that was hard to misinterpret.

definition: To deter someone is to discourage or prevent them from acting. To deter a thing is to stop or limit it.
example: The heavy fines aim to deter people from dumping garbage here.

definition: Ilk is a noun that means "sort" or "kind." It is usually used in short phrases with and or of, as in "and that ilk" and "of their ilk."
example: The hole beneath the stairs of the cabin's porch allows in squirrels, woodchucks, and other creatures of that ilk.

definition: Jerkwater means “remote and unimportant.” It is often used to describe a small town, village, etc., that is out in the country far from cities. Jerkwater can also mean “trivial.”
example: I grew up in a jerkwater town in the middle of nowhere.

definition: To rue something is to feel penitence, remorse, or regret for it. Rue is often used in the phrase "rue the day."
example: I rue the day I signed that infernal contract.

definition: Heinous describes things—such as acts, deeds, or crimes—that are hatefully or shockingly evil, or in other words, deserving of hate or contempt.
example: The former dictator will stand trial for the role he played in his government’s heinous treatment of political dissidents.

definition: Paraphernalia can refer to objects or items that are used to do a particular activity, as well as objects or items that are typically associated with a particular activity, subject, etc. The word can also refer generally to personal belongings.
example: Jordan’s childhood bedroom was filled with hockey paraphernalia.

definition: In general contexts, winnowing is about removing what is not wanted. One can winnow items, or one can winnow something that has items: you winnow less important or less desirable items by removing them from a group, list, etc.; and you winnow a list or group by removing the less important or less desirable items from it. In agricultural contexts, to winnow chaff (unwanted seed coverings and other debris) is to remove it from grain by throwing the grain up in the air and letting the wind blow the unwanted parts away.
example: The search committee is finding it extremely difficult to winnow the list of job candidates down to three finalists; many of them are highly qualified.

definition: Approbation is a formal word that refers to praise or approval.
example: Their plan to rewild portions of the city’s parks has won the approbation of the mayor.

definition: By and large is another way of saying "in general" or "on the whole."
example: By and large, I like the way things have gone.

definition: The word dally has a number of meanings. To dally can be to physically linger or dawdle, or to waste time. Dally may also mean "to act playfully," especially in a romantic sense, or "to deal with something lightly or in a way that is not serious."
example: Three members of the hiking group were dallying and didn't arrive at the overlook until others were already starting to head back to the trailhead.

definition: A nebula is a large cloud of interstellar gas or dust. In nontechnical use, the word nebula also refers to a galaxy other than the Milky Way.
example: We were eventually able to see the nebula through the telescope.

definition: Liminal is a formal word most often used to describe an intermediate state, phase, or condition. It can also describe something that is barely perceptible or barely capable of eliciting a response.
example: The essay presents an image of the border region as a liminal zone where one culture blends into another.

definition: Succor is a literary term meaning "something that you do or give to help someone who is suffering or in a difficult situation."
example: We see it as our duty to give succor to those in need.

definition: Callow is a synonym of immature used to describe someone, especially a young person, who does not have much experience and does not know how to behave like an adult. Like the word immature, callow is often used disapprovingly.
example: The novel’s plot involves a callow youth who eventually learns the value of hard work and self-reliance.

definition: To fraternize with someone is to be friendly with them or to spend time with them in a friendly way. Fraternize is often, though not always, used in situations where such friendly behavior is considered wrong or improper, as in “fraternizing with the enemy.”
example: The boss warned that fraternizing with the junior employees could be a risky career move for a manager.

definition: Something described as chockablock is very full or tightly packed.
example: Their mantel is chockablock with knickknacks collected from their travels to all fifty states.

definition: Ethos refers to the guiding beliefs of a person, group, or organization.
example: The company made environmental awareness part of its business ethos.

definition: Someone described as ambivalent has or displays very different feelings (such as love and hate) about someone or something at the same time.
example: Aya was ambivalent about starting her first year away at college—excited for the new opportunities that awaited but sad to leave her friends and family back home.

definition: Memento is a synonym of souvenir; it refers to something that is kept as a reminder of a person, place, or thing.
example: The box on the shelf in her closet is filled with mementos of her basketball career—awards, newspaper clippings, team photographs, and her old uniform.

definition: To vilify someone or something is to say or write very harsh and critical things about them. The word is a synonym of defame.
example: They were vilified in the press for their comments.

definition: Replete is an adjective used to describe things as "fully or abundantly provided or filled," "abundantly fed," "stout," or "complete."
example: The book is replete with photographs.

definition: A gridiron is a football field. The word gridiron is also used sometimes to refer to a grate for broiling food (as in “put the steaks on the gridiron”) or something consisting of or covered with a network (as in “a gridiron of streets and avenues”).
example: The book recounts the quarterback’s most glorious moments on the gridiron.

definition: Someone or something ensconced is firmly placed or hidden. Ensconce can be a synonym of shelter and conceal, or of establish and settle.
example: The sculpture is safely ensconced behind glass.

definition: Cronyism is the unfair practice by a powerful person (such as a politician) of giving jobs and other favors to friends without regard for their qualifications.
example: City residents are pushing back against cronyism and corruption in their local government.

definition: Incandescent has literal and figurative meanings. Its literal meanings relate to heat and light; it describes something that is white or glowing because of great heat, and also something (like a light bulb) that produces bright light when heated. In figurative use, incandescent relates to several kinds of brilliance. Something or someone described as incandescent can be very impressive, successful, or intelligent, or simply happy and lively. In British English, incandescent can also describe someone or something feeling or showing great anger.
example: The invention of the incandescent bulb in the 19th century ushered in the age of electric lighting.

definition: Skirl means "to play the bagpipes" when the subject of the sentence is a person, as in "the piper skirled." When bagpipes are the subject (as in "the bagpipes skirled"), skirl means "to emit the high shrill tone of the chanter," with chanter referring to the reed pipe on which the bagpipe's melody is played.
example: The attention of the parade-goers was fully captured the instant the bagpipers began skirling.

definition: Something described as byzantine (or Byzantine) is very complicated, secret, and hard to understand. In its most literal (and always capitalized) sense, Byzantine describes that which is "of, relating to, or characteristic of the ancient city of Byzantium."
example: The company's byzantine accounting practices have gotten it into trouble with the government.

definition: Mise-en-scène can refer to the setting of a play, movie, etc., or it can refer to the physical or social setting in which something real occurs or develops.
example: The mise-en-scène is spare, comprising only a table and two chairs under a low-hanging light.

definition: Clement is a formal word used to describe weather that is mild, or in other words, neither too hot nor too cold. Clement is also sometimes used to describe someone who is inclined to be merciful or lenient, as in “a clement judge.”
example: Although she loves visiting the northeast, Sue prefers to live in places with a more clement climate, without heavy snows or high heating bills.

definition: To lollygag is to spend time doing things that are not useful or serious, or in other words, to fool around and waste time.
example: Stop lollygagging and get to work!

definition: Propinquity is a formal word that typically refers to nearness in place or time, making it a synonym of proximity. It can also be used as a synonym of kinship to refer to the state of being related to others by blood.
example: The geographical propinquity of these ancient cultures explains many of the architectural similarities.

definition: Fallacious is a formal word that typically describes something, such as an argument or assumption, that is false or inaccurate and that tends to mislead or deceive others.
example: The notion that disease is caused by malign spirits was known to be fallacious long before the advent of germ theory.

definition: To attenuate something is to make it weaker or less in amount, effect, or force.
example: The switch from the clack of typewriters to the quiet tap of computer keyboards greatly attenuated the noise level of the office.

definition: Jeremiad refers to a long cautionary or angry rant about something. It can also refer to a similarly prolonged lamentation, or expression of great sorrow or deep sadness.
example: His jeremiad about trivial problems with the campsite didn’t go over well with his friends.

definition: Newfangled describes something that has been recently invented or developed, and usually implies that this new thing is difficult for some to understand.
example: The neighbors are always showing off their new gadgets and tools, but I feel no need for those newfangled contraptions.

definition: Dearth refers to a lack or inadequate supply. It is usually followed by of.
example: There is no dearth of opportunities for volunteers at the fair.

definition: In general contexts, something that ossifies becomes hardened or conventional and opposed to change. In medical contexts, something that ossifies (such as cartilage) forms or is transformed into bone.
example: I asked if she'd reconsider her position, but her opinions on the matter have clearly ossified.

definition: A propensity is a strong natural tendency to do something.
example: As a child, she had a strong propensity for mischief.

definition: Lethargic describes people who feel a lack of energy or a lack of interest in doing things. It is sometimes used figuratively, as in "a sluggish and lethargic economy."
example: The jet lag from their weeklong international honeymoon left them feeling lethargic for a few days.

definition: To impugn something, such as a person's integrity, judgment, etc., is to attack or oppose it as false or lacking integrity.
example: The defense attorneys did their best to impugn the motives of the prosecution’s key witnesses.

definition: Copious is a synonym of abundant and plentiful. It is always used before a noun to describe something very large in amount or number.
example: The pie was served with a copious amount of ice cream.

definition: Tchotchke refers to a small object used for decoration. It's a synonym of knickknack and trinket.
example: Their shelves were cluttered with tchotchkes from a lifetime of vacations.

definition: Someone or something that is encumbered is burdened or weighed down (as in “tourists encumbered by heavy luggage”) or hindered (as in “negotiations encumbered by a lack of trust”).
example: The children found it difficult to climb down the river's steep embankment, encumbered as they were by inner tubes and towels.

definition: A gadabout is a person who flits about in social activity, as by going to many places and social events for pleasure.
example: She was a gadabout who was rarely home, and her tiny apartment was cluttered with playbills and other souvenirs of her adventures.

definition: Sentient is a formal term that typically describes beings conscious of or responsive to the sensations of seeing, hearing, feeling, tasting, or smelling.
example: An avid gardener, Dorothy has recently been absorbed in books that examine the question of whether, and to what degree, plants are sentient.

definition: An iota is an infinitesimal amount of something. The word iota is used synonymously with the etymologically related jot, and by its oldest definition refers to the 9th letter of the Greek alphabet.
example: There's not an iota of doubt regarding the defendant's guilt.

definition: To vitiate something is to ruin it or render it ineffective.
example: A single inaccuracy in the spreadsheet that supported the data vitiated the entire proposal.

definition: Durable describes people or things that last, or remain strong and in good condition over a long period of time. It is often used figuratively, as in "a durable athlete."
example: The fabric was durable enough to withstand chewing from the family dog.

definition: Acumen refers to keenness and depth of perception, discernment, or discrimination—in other words, the ability to think clearly and make good decisions, especially in practical matters.
example: The fictional detective possesses a superior acumen that enables her to solve the most bizarre and puzzling of mysteries.

definition: Someone or something described as fusty is rigidly old-fashioned. Fusty is also used as a synonym of musty to describe things that are full of dust and unpleasant, stale odors.
example: Wanda is quick to admit that the music she prefers is fusty, as it excludes pretty much anything recorded after 1960.

definition: Reifying is about considering or representing something abstract as a material or concrete thing. If you reify a concept or idea you somehow give it definite content and form.
example: The tense personal dynamic between the two musicians was reified by the dissonant yet captivating music they made together.

definition: Balayage is a technique by which a colorist creates highlights or lowlights in a person's hair by painting freehand using long, sweeping strokes. Balayage may also refer to the highlights or lowlights produced by this technique.
example: The stylist was lauded for his skill in balayage.

definition: Capricious is a formal word that describes someone or something governed or characterized by impulsivity or unpredictability.
example: The employees were at the mercy of a capricious manager who always seemed to impose deadlines at the last minute.

definition: Hoopla refers to talk or writing that is designed to get people excited about or interested in something, often with the implication that the person using the word does not find the thing exciting or interesting.
example: Marvin didn’t understand all of the hoopla surrounding the new frozen yogurt shop in his neighborhood.

definition: Parry has two basic meanings. To parry can be to defend yourself by turning away from or pushing aside a weapon, assault, etc., or to evade something, such as a question, especially by using a clever response.
example: Players of the game must unfailingly parry blows from multiple varied attackers while progressing through a series of worlds.

definition: Extemporaneous describes something that is made up or done without special preparation. It is usually used to describe public speaking.
example: Now a seasoned professional, Abby is no longer unnerved when asked to make the occasional extemporaneous speech.

definition: Midriff refers to the area around a person’s middle, that is, the front of their body between the chest and the waist.
example: Even the store’s winter line of clothing includes a number of midriff-baring tops, albeit paired with oversized cardigans or flannel shirts.

definition: Impeccable describes that which is free from fault, error, or blame. It is a synonym of flawless.
example: Although the restaurant was a bit expensive, we found its memorable cuisine, luxurious decor, and impeccable service to be well worth the price.

definition: To purport is to claim to be or do a particular thing when this claim may not be true.
example: The report purports to be objective, but its bias is clear.

definition: To cast aspersion (or aspersions) on someone is to criticize them harshly or unfairly: aspersion is defined as "a false or misleading charge meant to harm someone's reputation, or the act of making such a charge." Aspersion may also refer to a sprinkling with water, especially in religious ceremonies.
example: Melissa believed that Roger had unjustly cast aspersions on the quality of her research.

definition: Dulcet is a formal word used to describe sounds that are pleasant to hear. It is often used in the phrase “dulcet tones.”
example: Jolie recalled warm memories of falling asleep to the dulcet tones of her grandmother’s lullabies.

definition: Jurisprudence is a formal word that typically refers to the science or philosophy of law, or to a system or body of law.
example: An undergraduate class on jurisprudence inspired her decision to go to law school.

definition: Herald is a verb meaning "to give notice of"; it is synonymous with announce, publicize, and foreshadow. Herald may also mean "to greet especially with enthusiasm."
example: The appearance of robins heralded the advent of spring.

definition: Fealty is an old-fashioned and somewhat literary word that refers to intense loyalty or fidelity to a person, group, etc. More narrowly, fealty refers to the fidelity of a vassal or feudal tenant to their lord.
example: Authors who inspire such fealty can guarantee a publisher good sales, no matter the quality of the books they write.

definition: Someone described as sanctimonious behaves as though they are morally superior to others. Language or behavior that suggests the same kind of moral superiority can also be described as sanctimonious.
example: While the subject matter was interesting, I found the presenter’s sanctimonious tone rather distracting.

definition: A catastrophe is never a good thing. Catastrophe can refer to a momentous tragic event, an utter failure, a violent and sudden change in a feature of the earth, or a violent usually destructive natural event.
example: Despite her careful planning, the party turned out to be a catastrophe.

definition: Extenuate is a formal word that is most often used to mean “to lessen the strength or effect of something, such as a risk.” In legal use, to extenuate a crime, offense, etc., is to lessen or to try to lessen its seriousness or extent by making partial excuses.
example: Developers are trying to extenuate the various risks associated with the product.

definition: Visage is a formal word that refers to someone’s face or facial expression, or to the general appearance of something.
example: Manny was surprised to see the smiling visage of his childhood friend, now running for the state senate, beaming down from a billboard.

definition: Someone or something described as amiable is friendly and agreeable.
example: Both children have amiable dispositions, which makes them easy to travel with.

definition: To nonplus someone is to perplex them, or in other words, to cause them to be at a loss as to what to say, think, or do.
example: The stranger's odd question about the town where my grandfather was born nonplussed me.

definition: Tomfoolery is a word with an old-fashioned sound to it that refers to playful or silly behavior.
example: The antics in the play itself apparently inspired tomfoolery behind the scenes as well, as cast members constantly played practical jokes on one another.

definition: Otiose is a formal word typically used to describe either something that serves no useful purpose, or something that has no use or effect.
example: I enjoyed the storyline, but was bothered by the otiose punctuation.

definition: To harry someone or something is to harass or torment them by or as if by constant attack.
example: The visiting team harried the home team relentlessly during the first quarter.

definition: Limpid describes things that are perfectly transparent or clear, or that are simple in style.
example: Though the stream was deep, flecks and shimmers in the sand shone up through its limpid water.

definition: Coterie refers to an intimate and often exclusive group of people with a unifying common interest or purpose.
example: The mayor arrived at the meeting with a coterie of advisors.

definition: Something described as eclectic, such as a collection or a person's tastes, includes things taken from many different sources.
example: The collection includes an eclectic mix of historical artifacts.

definition: Bilk is typically applied in contexts relating to fraud and deceit. It can mean "to cheat out of something valuable," or "to evade payment of or to," or "to obtain something by defrauding someone."
example: Prosecutors contend that the defendant bilked hundreds of investors out of their life savings.

definition: Fountainhead is a word usually encountered in literary contexts that refers to the origin or source of something.
example: Ragtime, popularized by such performers as Scott Joplin and Eubie Blake, is considered one of the musical fountainheads of jazz.

definition: Ungainly usually describes someone or something moving in an awkward or clumsy way, or the awkward, clumsy movements themselves. It can also describe an object that is difficult to handle (especially because of being large or heavy), or someone or something that has an awkward appearance.
example: While seals are ungainly on land, they are beautifully agile swimmers.

definition: Respite refers to a short period of time when someone is able to stop doing something that is difficult or unpleasant, or when something difficult or unpleasant stops or is delayed.
example: The long weekend provided a nice respite from the pressures of her job.

definition: To dicker is to talk or argue with someone about the conditions of a purchase, agreement, or contract.
example: My favorite thing about flea markets is dickering over prices.

definition: Someone described as swole is extremely muscular. In other words, they have a physique enhanced by bodybuilding exercises.
example: Her New Year’s resolution was to get swole, so she signed up with a personal trainer and committed to working out every day.

definition: A mogul is a powerful and influential person.
example: The music mogul's latest album has been nominated for several awards.

definition: Castigate is a formal word that means "to criticize harshly."
example: He was widely castigated for earning millions of dollars in bonuses as the company he was leading slid into insolvency.

definition: Patriot refers to a person who loves and strongly supports or fights for their country.
example: Addy enjoyed looking at old photographs of her grandmother, a patriot who served in the Women’s Army Auxiliary Corps during World War II, in uniform.

definition: Something described as insuperable is impossible to gain control of, solve, or overcome.
example: The book tells the inspiring story of a group of people who achieved a great deal despite nearly insuperable obstacles.

definition: A glade is a grassy open space in a forest.
example: She felt the most at ease outdoors, often taking delight in the peaceful glades she came across on her hikes.

definition: Abhor is synonymous with loathe. Something or someone who is abhorred is regarded with extreme disgust or hatred.
example: Mariah is an animal rights activist who abhors any and all mistreatment of animals.

definition: Kudos refers to praise someone receives because of an act or achievement, or to fame and renown that results from an act or achievement.
example: Kudos to everyone who helped clean up the community garden.

definition: Fecund is a formal word that typically describes a person, animal, or plant that is producing or able to produce many offspring. It is synonymous with fertile and fruitful. Fecund is also used figuratively to describe something especially intellectually productive or inventive, as in "a fecund source of ideas."
example: The farm’s fecund fields abounded with produce.

definition: Deference refers to respect and esteem that is appropriate to show to someone, such as a superior or elder. Something done in deference to, or out of deference to, someone or something is done in order to show respect for the opinions or influence of that person or thing.
example: The children were taught to show proper deference to their elders.

definition: Cardinal is an adjective used to describe things—usually abstract things such as rules or principles—that are of basic or main importance. The word is also used, especially in the phrase “cardinal sin,” with the meaning “very serious or grave.”
example: “Seek out multiple sources” is a cardinal rule of good news reporting.

definition: Zero-sum describes something, such as a game, mentality, or situation, in which any gain corresponds directly with an equivalent loss.
example: Dividing up the budget is a zero-sum game.

definition: Remuneration is a formal word that refers to an amount of money paid to someone for a service, loss, or expense, or to the act of paying such an amount. It is synonymous with recompense and pay.
example: The actor was offered a modest speaking fee by the host as remuneration for giving her speech at the awards ceremony.

definition: Clandestine describes something done secretly, or in a private place or way.
example: The wedding was a clandestine affair in Las Vegas.

definition: A polemic is a strong written or spoken attack against someone else’s opinions, beliefs, practices, etc.
example: Her book is a fierce polemic against societal inequalities.

definition: Supersede is a verb meaning "to take the place of (someone or something that is considered old, inferior, or no longer useful)." It is used synonymously with replace and displace.
example: This edition of the manual supersedes the previous one.

definition: A person described as vulnerable in a general way is someone who is easily hurt or harmed physically, mentally, or emotionally. Vulnerable can also describe a person, group, or thing that is open to attack, harm, or damage. Both senses of vulnerable are often followed by the preposition to.
example: It is common to feel especially vulnerable in the wake of major change.

definition: Hue and cry refers to a clamor of alarm or protest in response to something. It can also be used as a synonym of hubbub to refer to general noise or uproar.
example: After the popular professor was fired by the college, there was such a hue and cry from students that the administration was forced to reconsider its decision.

definition: Jubilee usually refers to a special anniversary or a celebration of such an anniversary. It can also refer generally to a season of celebration or act of rejoicing, or to a religious song of African Americans referring to a time of future happiness.
example: My grandparents will be celebrating their golden jubilee this year—as Grandpa puts it, "50 years of wedded bliss and occasional blisters."

definition: A brainiac is a very intelligent person.
example: Her ability to solve almost any puzzle within minutes secured her place as the brainiac of the family.

definition: Something described as apocryphal is of doubtful authenticity; the term is often applied to stories or legends that are often repeated but likely not true. Apocryphal can also describe something resembling or relating to the Apocrypha, the ancient Jewish books that are not part of the Hebrew Bible but are considered canonical in Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches. In the biblical use, the word is often capitalized.
example: The legend of how the song was fully composed while the singer was in a deep fever state is probably apocryphal.

definition: Paradigm is a formal word that refers to a pattern or example, and especially to an outstandingly clear or typical example or archetype. It can also refer to a theory or group of ideas about how something should be done, made, or thought about.
example: Her latest book provides us with a new paradigm for modern biography.

definition: Unbeknownst means “without being known about by (a specified person or group of people).”
example: Unbeknownst to the students, the teacher had entered the room.

definition: To rebuff something, such as an offer or suggestion, is to reject or criticize it sharply. One can also rebuff a person by rudely rejecting or refusing them.
example: When their request was immediately rebuffed by upper management, the staff was left frustrated yet also more determined.

definition: When used literally, lodestone refers to the mineral magnetite, a magnetic iron ore. Lodestone is also used figuratively to refer to something that, like a magnet, strongly attracts things.
example: The city is a lodestone for aspiring musicians of all genres.

definition: Efficacious is a formal word used to describe something—often a treatment, medicine, or remedy—that has the power to produce a desired result or effect.
example: Companies like to tout the number of efficacious natural ingredients in their beauty products.

definition: To foment something, such as hostility or opposition, is to cause it, or try to cause it, to grow or develop. Foment is used synonymously with incite.
example: Rumors that the will was a fake fomented distrust between the two families.

definition: Tractable is used to describe someone or something that is easily led, managed, taught, or controlled.
example: This new approach should make the problem more tractable.

definition: Consternation is a formal word that refers to a strong feeling of surprise or sudden disappointment that causes confusion.
example: The candidate caused consternation among his supporters by changing positions on a key issue.

definition: When you go incognito, your true identity is kept secret (as through the use of a different name or a disguise). Incognito can be used either as an adverb or an adjective with the same meaning.
example: The food critic made an incognito visit to the restaurant.

definition: To gossip is to talk about the personal lives of other people.
example: The two siblings often gossip with each other about their neighbors via texting.

definition: Moxie can refer to courage and determination (aka nerve), energy and pep (aka verve), or know-how (as, say, reflected in one’s oeuvre).
example: They showed a lot of moxie in questioning their company’s policy.

definition: Someone described as affluent has a large amount of money and owns many expensive things. Something, such as a place or institution, described as affluent is similarly rich or wealthy.
example: The affluent suburb sports some of the finest public schools in the county owing to its considerable tax base.

definition: Meliorism refers to the belief that the world tends to improve and that humans can aid its betterment.
example: Her belief in meliorism has given her a positive outlook on life.

definition: To deride someone or something is to subject them to usually harsh and bitter insults or criticism.
example: Although derided by classmates for his insistence that he would be a millionaire by the age of 25, he achieved his goal when his Internet startup went public.

definition: Incidence refers to the number of times something happens or develops—in other words, the rate at which something occurs.
example: The neighborhood boasts excellent schools and a low incidence of crime.

definition: Someone described as svelte is considered slender or thin in an attractive or graceful way. Svelte can also be used to describe something sleek, such as a vehicle or an article of clothing.
example: The svelte dancer seemed to float across the stage.

definition: Foist, which is almost always used with on or upon, is used when someone forces another person to accept something, usually something that is not good or is not wanted. Foist can also mean “to pass off as genuine or worthy.”
example: I don’t want to foist anything on you, but if you like this old quilt you’re welcome to have it.

definition: Dynasty refers to a group (such as a team, family, etc.) that is very powerful or successful for a long period of time. It is also often used for a family of rulers who rule over a country for a long period of time, as well as the period of time when a particular dynasty is in power.
example: The team’s draft picks reflected the ownership’s strategy of building a long-term football dynasty.

definition: Obstreperous is a formal word that describes people or things that stubbornly resist control; in this use it’s a synonym of unruly. A person or thing described as obstreperous may also be defiantly or aggressively noisy.
example: The moment the paper airplane landed, the instructor addressed the unruly class, telling them in the harshest tone that obstreperous conduct would not be tolerated.

definition: In literal use, gadfly refers to any of various flies (such as a horsefly, botfly, or warble fly) that bite or annoy livestock. Gadfly is most popular in figurative use, however, where it refers to someone who provokes or annoys other people especially by persistent criticism.
example: The journalist was known as a gadfly for exposing hypocrisy in politics.

definition: To glean is to gather or collect something bit by bit, or in a gradual way. Glean can also be used to mean “to search (something) carefully” and “to find out.”
example: Neil has a collection of antique tools gleaned from flea markets and garage sales.

definition: Symposium can refer either to a formal meeting at which experts discuss a particular topic, or to a collection of articles on a particular subject. Symposium has two plural forms: symposia and symposiums.
example: Professors and graduate students attended a three-day symposium on climate change.

definition: To countermand an order is to revoke it, especially by giving a new order.
example: Orders to blow up the bridge were countermanded by local officials.

definition: If someone or something is appealingly lively and enthusiastic, they may also be described as ebullient.
example: Akua's ebullient personality made her the life of the party.

definition: Panoply is a formal word that refers to a group or collection that is impressive either because of its size or because it includes so many different kinds of people or things.
example: The new website offers shoppers a panoply of snack foods, soft drinks, and other treats from around the world.

definition: To belie something is to give a false idea or impression of it. Belie can also mean "to show (something) to be false or wrong."
example: Martin's easy banter and relaxed attitude belied his nervousness.

definition: A neophyte is a person who has just started learning or doing something.
example: As an acting neophyte, Femi took a while to adjust to his newfound Hollywood fame.

definition: An effort, action, or emotion described as futile has no result or effect, and therefore serves no useful purpose.
example: City officials attempted to stifle the scandal, but their efforts were futile.

definition: To sequester a person or group is to keep them separate or apart from other people. Sequester is also often used to mean “to bind or absorb (carbon dioxide) as part of a larger chemical process or compound.”
example: The jury was sequestered until a verdict was reached.

definition: Artifice refers to dishonest or insincere behavior or speech that is meant to deceive someone. It can also be used to mean "clever or artful skill."
example: We found ourselves tremendously moved by his apology, which he made without artifice or pretense.

definition: Something described as lucrative produces money or wealth.
example: The author parlayed the success of her books into a lucrative second career as a public speaker.

definition: Debacle is usually used synonymously with fiasco to mean “a complete failure.” It can also refer to a great disaster (though typically not one that causes significant suffering or loss).
example: After the debacle of his first novel, he had trouble getting a publisher for his next book.

definition: To wane is to become smaller or less, or in other words, to decrease in size, extent, or degree.
example: The national scandal caused her popularity to wane.

definition: A caveat is an explanation or warning that should be remembered when you are doing or thinking about something. In legal contexts, caveat refers to a notice to a court or judicial officer to suspend a proceeding until the opposition can be heard.
example: All investment advice should come with a caveat: the stock market is impossible to predict with absolute accuracy.

definition: To instigate something is to cause it to happen or begin by urging or goading others. Instigate is a synonym of provoke.
example: The pair was accused of instigating a plot to oust the newly elected mayor.

definition: Torrid can be used to describe something that is literally hot (such as a region near the Earth’s equator) or figuratively hot (such as a romance).
example: The tabloids were relentless in covering every minor detail of the celebrity couple’s torrid affair.

definition: To zhuzh something up is to improve its flavor or appearance by way of a small improvement, adjustment, or addition.
example: He likes to zhuzh up his outfits with brightly-colored ties.

definition: To bogart something is to use or consume it without sharing.
example: Nelson advised his friends not to bogart all the snacks before the rest of the party guests arrived.

definition: Grudging is an adjective used to describe something that is said, done, or given unwillingly or reluctantly. It can also describe someone who is unwilling or reluctant to do something.
example: Her theories have begun to win grudging acceptance in the scientific community.

definition: A reputation is the common opinion that people have about someone or something. Reputation can also refer to a positive position that someone or something has in public esteem or regard.
example: She's earned a reputation as a first-class playwright.

definition: To extemporize means to do something extemporaneously—in other words, to improvise.
example: A good talk show host must be able to extemporize when interviews don’t go as planned.

definition: Something, such as a sound, that is described as plangent is loud, deep, and often expressive of sadness or suffering. The word is a synonym of plaintive.
example: The campers were awoken by the plangent howl of a coyote off in the distance.

definition: To proliferate is to increase quickly in number or amount.
example: Problems have proliferated in recent months; every day seems to present a new challenge that needs sorting out.

definition: Something described as agrarian has to do with farms and farming.
example: Joan hopes to leave city life behind and move to a more agrarian region where she plans to raise lambs and grow heirloom vegetables.

definition: Melee refers to a confused fight or struggle, especially one involving hand-to-hand combat.
example: What started as a verbal disagreement at the football game soon turned into a general melee involving scores of spectators.

definition: Forfend is used in contexts relating to some kind of real or pretended danger or other unpleasantness. In humorous and ironic use, forfend typically appears in the phrase “heaven forfend,” and, like “heaven forbid,” expresses a usually ironic desire that something not happen or be done. In general use, if you forfend something unwanted or undesirable, you ward it off or prevent it; and if you forfend yourself from or against something, you protect or preserve yourself from it.
example: Heaven forfend that people actually pick up dictionaries and read them!

definition: Something described as cohesive sticks together and forms something closely united. The word is usually used with abstract terms in phrases like "a cohesive social unit" or "a cohesive look/aesthetic." Cohesive can also be used to describe something, such as the design of a room or the plot of a movie, that is coherent—in other words, logically or consistently ordered.
example: The couple chose their wedding colors and designs carefully to make sure everything had a cohesive look.

definition: A demagogue is a political leader who tries to get support by making use of popular prejudices, as well as by making false claims and promises and using arguments based on emotion rather than reason.
example: His opponent called him a bigoted demagogue for demonizing those who don't intend to vote for him.

definition: Inviolable is a formal term that is used to describe something too important to be ignored or treated with disrespect.
example: She considers herself a person with inviolable moral standards.

definition: Ken refers to someone’s range of perception, knowledge, or understanding, and is most often used in phrases like “beyond/outside/within one’s ken.”
example: The author advised the aspiring writers in the crowd to develop an authoritative voice by sticking to subjects within their ken.

definition: Assail has a number of meanings relating to violent or powerful confrontations. It can be a straightforward synonym of assault, as in "assailed by armed robbers," or it can mean "to oppose, challenge, or criticize harshly and forcefully," as in "citizens assailing the proposed changes." It can also mean "to trouble or afflict in a way that threatens to overwhelm," as in "assailed by fears." Assail can also apply to powerful perceptions: a smell that assails you, for example, is strongly noticeable and usually unpleasant. Occasionally, assail is used to mean "to encounter, undertake, or confront energetically," as in "with a deadline fast approaching, we assailed the project with renewed vigor."
example: Most worthwhile achievements require that one persevere even when assailed by doubts.

definition: An homage is something that is done to honor someone or something. It is often used with the word pay (as in “pay homage”) to mean “to respect or honor.”
example: Her latest book is an homage to her favorite city.

definition: Tendentious is a formal word used disapprovingly to describe someone or something expressing a strongly biased point of view in a way that may cause argument.
example: The book proved to be a tendentious account of the town's history, written to rescue the reputation of one of its less scrupulous founders.

definition: To burgeon is to grow or develop quickly—in other words to flourish, blossom or sprout.
example: The trout population in the stream has burgeoned since the town implemented its laws against overfishing.

definition: An exodus is a situation in which many people leave a place at the same time—in other words a mass departure or emigration.
example: The resort town eagerly anticipated the mass exodus from the cities to its beaches as summer approached.

definition: Something described as palpable is obvious and notable. Palpable may also be used as a synonym of tangible to describe something that can be perceived by one's sense of touch.
example: The tension in the courtroom was palpable as the jury foreman stood to announce the verdict.

definition: Noblesse oblige refers to the idea that people who have high social rank or wealth should be helpful and generous to people of lower rank or to people who are poor.
example: As the inheritor of a great fortune, he was raised to have a strong sense of noblesse oblige, not only volunteering and donating to charity, but advocating for structural change to address inequality.

definition: An act or manner described as gingerly is very cautious or careful.
example: It’s a delicate subject, and we need to approach it with gingerly care and tact.

definition: To underwhelm someone is to fail to impress or excite them.
example: Despite the hype, the movie underwhelmed most reviewers, who criticized its slow pace and poor special effects.

definition: Qua is a preposition used in formal speech or writing that means “in the capacity or character of (someone or something).” It is used synonymously with as to indicate that someone or something is being referred to or thought about in a particular way.
example: The artist qua artist is less interesting to me than the artist as a human being.

definition: Circumlocution refers to the use of many words to say something that could be said more clearly and directly with fewer words. Usually encountered in formal speech and writing, circumlocution can also refer to speech that is intentionally evasive.
example: The judge coughed and pointed to her watch, clearly impatient with the attorney's tiresome circumlocutions in defense of his client.

definition: Something considered inalienable is impossible to take away or give up.
example: The American ethos is built on the belief that life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness are inalienable rights.

definition: To purloin is to take something that belongs to someone else—that is, to steal it. Purloin is much more formal-sounding than steal, but is often—though not always—encountered in humorous contexts, suggesting that the theft is not serious.
example: The puppy managed to purloin a few cookies from the plate when no one was looking.

definition: A furlong is a unit of distance equal to 220 yards (about 201 meters), and is used chiefly in horse racing.
example: To win the Kentucky Derby, a Thoroughbred must run 10 furlongs, or one and 1/4 miles.

definition: A person may be described as brusque when they are talking or behaving in a very direct, brief, and unfriendly way. Brusque can also describe speech that is noticeably short and abrupt.
example: We knew something was wrong when our normally easygoing professor was brusque and impatient with our class.

definition: Surfeit is a formal word that refers to an amount or supply that is too much or more than you need. It is synonymous with the word excess.
example: The organization ended up with a surfeit of volunteers who simply got in each other's way.

definition: To discomfit someone is to make them confused or upset. Discomfit is a formal synonym of the also formal (but slightly less so) disconcert.
example: Jacob was discomfited by the new employee’s forward, probing questions.

definition: A vicarious emotion or experience is one felt by watching, hearing about, or reading about someone else rather than by doing something yourself.
example: He felt a vicarious thrill as his daughter crossed the stage to accept her diploma.

definition: Aegis is a formal word that refers to the power to protect, control, or support something or someone. It is often used in the phrase under the aegis of.
example: The issue will be decided under the aegis of an international organization.

definition: To describe something, such as an idea or remark, as fatuous is to say that it is foolish or silly rather than sensible or logical.
example: Our hopes for an apology and a reasonable explanation for the error were met with fatuous platitudes.

definition: Conjecture is a formal synonym of the verb guess that means “to form an opinion or idea without proof or sufficient evidence.”
example: Some scientists have conjectured that Jupiter’s moon Europa could sustain life.

definition: Redoubt can refer specifically to a small building or area that provides soldiers with protection from attack, or more broadly to any safe or protected place, whether literal or figurative.
example: A massive stone redoubt at the entrance of the bay guarded the city.

definition: Something or someone described as meticulous shows extreme or excessive care in the consideration or treatment of details.
example: He is meticulous about keeping accurate records.

definition: Praxis is a formal word referring to the practical application of a theory—in other words, what one does to act on a theory (such as feminist theory) to which one is committed. Praxis is also used synonymously with action or practice to refer to the exercise of an art, science, or skill, or to customary conduct within a given sphere.
example: Many gardeners promote composting as being good environmental praxis.

definition: To lambaste something or someone is to criticize them very harshly. Lambaste is also sometimes used as a synonym of beat meaning “to assault.”
example: The coach lambasted the team for its poor play.

definition: Ethereal means "of or relating to the regions beyond the earth" or "of or resembling heaven." It can also mean "lacking material substance" and "relating to, containing, or resembling a chemical ether."
example: The windows give the church an ethereal glow.

definition: Shambles refers to a place or state in which there is great confusion, disorder, or destruction.
example: The house party they had over the weekend left the entire living room in shambles.

definition: Expiate is a formal word that typically means “to atone or make amends for something, such as a sin or offense.”
example: Although the editorial had characterized the mayor's failure to disclose the details of the meeting as a lapse that could not be expiated, many of the city's citizens seemed ready to forgive all.

definition: Something haphazard has no apparent plan, order, or direction.
example: Considering the haphazard way you measured the ingredients, it's a wonder the cookies came out this good.

definition: Braggadocio refers to brash and self-confident boasting—that is, the annoying or exaggerated talk of someone who is trying to sound very proud or brave.
example: His braggadocio hid the fact that he felt personally inadequate.

definition: To flout something, such as a law or rule, is to treat it with contemptuous disregard. A teenager flouting a curfew, for example, will not hide the fact that they are out past the time they are required to be home.
example: The court found that the company had continued to flout the law despite multiple warnings.

definition: In general use, auxiliary describes someone or something available to provide extra help, power, etc., when it is needed. In linguistics, an auxiliary verb (also called a “helping verb”) is used with another verb to do things like show a verb’s tense or form a question. In nautical contexts, auxiliary can describe a sailboat equipped with a supplementary inboard engine, or a vessel that provides supplementary assistance to other ships.
example: The auditorium has an auxiliary cooling system used only on particularly sweltering days.

definition: Kismet refers to a power that is believed to control what happens in the future. It is synonymous with both fate and destiny.
example: From the moment we met, we felt connected; we knew it was kismet.

definition: To genuflect is to kneel, or nearly kneel, on one knee and then rise again in worship or as an act of respect. In figurative use, genuflect means "to be humbly obedient or respectful."
example: Churchgoers genuflected before the altar.

definition: Megillah is slang for a long, involved story or account. Megillah can also refer to a complicated sequence of events, or it can be used as a synonym of ball of wax meaning “everything involved in what is under consideration.” All three senses of megillah are often preceded by the adjective whole.
example: Don’t worry about reciting the whole megillah from last night’s game; just give me the highlights.

definition: Pedantic describes someone or something that exhibits the characteristics of a pedant—that is, a person who often annoys other people by correcting small errors and giving too much attention to minor details. Pedantic also means “narrowly, stodgily, and often ostentatiously learned.”
example: Their habit of reminding fellow birders that the bird is called a “Canada goose” and not a “Canadian goose” came across as pedantic rather than helpful.

definition: When used with into, dragoon means "to force or convince someone to do something." Without into, dragoon means "to subjugate or persecute by harsh use of troops."
example: Employees complained that they had been dragooned into working overtime without adequate compensation.

definition: Scurrilous is a formal adjective that most often describes language that contains obscenities, abuse, or, especially, slander—that is, a false statement that damages a person’s reputation. Scurrilous can also describe someone who uses or tends to use scurrilous language, or it can describe a person or thing as evil or vulgar.
example: The press secretary made a point at the briefing not to address the scurrilous rumors surrounding the senator.

definition: Flora refers to all the plants that live in a particular area, time, period, or environment. It can also be used broadly to refer to plant, bacterial, or fungal life.
example: Lisa admired the aquatic flora in the pond as she gazed out at the horizon.

definition: To allege something is to assert it without proof or before proving it.
example: Consumer advocates allege that the company knew about the faulty switches but sold the product anyway.

definition: Something described as tawdry is cheap and gaudy in appearance or quality. Tawdry is also often used to describe something considered morally bad or distasteful, as in "a tawdry tale of political skulduggery."
example: Tawdry decorations cluttered the tiny house.

definition: Blarney refers to false but charming talk that often flatters the listener.
example: The bartender laughingly asked her gregarious patron if anyone ever believed his blarney.
